- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. ## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Supabase
Here are guidelines for using Supabase tools effectively:

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

If you have access to a local development environment with a filesystem and shell:
- Install the Supabase agent skill for critical development and security guidance: `npx skills add supabase/agent-skills` (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/ai-skills.md)
- Use the Supabase CLI (`supabase`) for local development workflows such as starting a local stack, managing migrations, and running edge functions locally (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development.md)
- Prefer local development and testing before applying changes to a remote project

If you are running in a web-only or remote environment without filesystem or shell access:
- Rely on the MCP tools directly for all Supabase interactions
- Use `apply_migration` carefully, as changes go directly to the remote project

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
im = Image.open("imgs/hi_page-16.png").convert("L")

dark = arr < 200

cols = np.where(dark.any(axis=0))[0]
print("row range with any dark pixel:", rows.min(), rows.max())
print("col range with any dark pixel:", cols.min(), cols.max())
# Look for the grid specifically: rows with many dark pixels (long horizontal lines spanning grid width)
row_counts = dark.sum(axis=1)

col_counts = dark.sum(axis=0)
candidate_cols = np.where(col_counts > 400)[0]
print("candidate grid cols (count>400): min/max", candidate_cols.min() if len(candidate_cols) else None, candidate_cols.max() if len(candidate_cols) else None, "n=",len(candidate_cols))

input.command:

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
NS = "{http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml}"
tree = ET.parse("pp1_bbox.xml")
root = tree.getroot()

pages = []
for page in root.iter(NS+"page"):
    w = float(page.get("width")); h = float(page.get("height"))
    lines = []
    for line in page.iter(NS+"line"):
        xs=[]; ys0=[]; ys1=[]; txt=[]
        for word in line.iter(NS+"word"):
            xs.append(float(word.get("xMin")))
            ys0.append(float(word.get("yMin")))
            ys1.append(float(word.get("yMax")))
            txt.append((word.text or "").strip())
        if txt:
            lines.append((min(ys0), max(ys1), min(xs), " ".join(txt)))
    pages.append((w,h,lines))

import pickle
with open("pages_lines.pkl","wb") as f:
    pickle.dump(pages, f)

for i,(w,h,lines) in enumerate(pages, start=1):
    print(f"=== PAGE {i} (w={w:.1f} h={h:.1f}) ===")
    for y0,y1,x0,txt in lines:
        print(f"  y[{y0:6.1f},{y1:6.1f}] x0={x0:6.1f}  {txt[:90]}")
EOF

def diagram_bbox(path, y0, y1, thresh=150, mincount=15, gap=6):

def topY(y_top):
    """convert top-origin pt coordinate to reportlab bottom-origin"""
    return PAGE_H - y_top

def wrap_line(c, text, font, size, max_width):
    """wrap a single logical line into multiple physical lines if too wide"""
    words = text.split(" ")
    lines = []
    cur = ""
    for w in words:
        trial = (cur + " " + w).strip()
        if pdfmetrics.stringWidth(trial, font, size) <= max_width or not cur:
            cur = trial
        else:
            lines.append(cur)
            cur = w
    if cur:
        lines.append(cur)
    return lines

def fit_and_draw(c, x0, x1, ytop_start, ytop_end, logical_lines,
                  font="DejaVu", max_size=10.5, min_size=6.0, leading_ratio=1.28,
                  align="left", first_bold=False):
    """Fit logical_lines (list of str) into the box, choosing largest font that fits."""
    width = x1 - x0
    height = ytop_end - ytop_start
    size = max_size
    while size >= min_size:
        leading = size * leading_ratio
        all_phys = []
        for ln in logical_lines:
            wrapped = wrap_line(c, ln, font, size, width)
            all_phys.extend(wrapped if wrapped else [""])
        total_h = len(all_phys) * leading
        if total_h <= height:
            break
        size -= 0.5
    else:
        size = min_size
        leading = size * leading_ratio
        all_phys = []
        for ln in logical_lines:
            wrapped = wrap_line(c, ln, font, size, width)
            all_phys.extend(wrapped if wrapped else [""])

    c.setFont(font, size)
    c.setFillColor(RED)
    y_top_cursor = ytop_start + leading * 0.85
    for i, ln in enumerate(all_phys):
        y_rl = topY(y_top_cursor)
        if align == "left":
            c.drawString(x0, y_rl, ln)
        elif align == "center":
            c.drawCentredString((x0 + x1) / 2.0, y_rl, ln)
        y_top_cursor += leading
    return size

def zone(c, page_zones_key, ztab, lines, **kw):
    x0, x1, y0, y1 = ztab[page_zones_key]
    fit_and_draw(c, x0, x1, y0, y1, lines, **kw)

def topY(y_top):
    """convert top-origin pt coordinate to reportlab bottom-origin"""
    return PAGE_H - y_top

def wrap_line(c, text, font, size, max_width):
    """wrap a single logical line into multiple physical lines if too wide"""
    words = text.split(" ")
    lines = []
    cur = ""
    for w in words:
        trial = (cur + " " + w).strip()
        if pdfmetrics.stringWidth(trial, font, size) <= max_width or not cur:
            cur = trial
        else:
            lines.append(cur)
            cur = w
    if cur:
        lines.append(cur)
    return lines

def fit_and_draw(c, x0, x1, ytop_start, ytop_end, logical_lines,
                  font="DejaVu", max_size=10.5, min_size=6.0, leading_ratio=1.28,
                  align="left", first_bold=False):
    """Fit logical_lines (list of str) into the box, choosing largest font that fits."""
    width = x1 - x0
    height = ytop_end - ytop_start
    size = max_size
    while size >= min_size:
        leading = size * leading_ratio
        all_phys = []
        for ln in logical_lines:
            wrapped = wrap_line(c, ln, font, size, width)
            all_phys.extend(wrapped if wrapped else [""])
        total_h = len(all_phys) * leading
        if total_h <= height:
            break
        size -= 0.5
    else:
        size = min_size
        leading = size * leading_ratio
        all_phys = []
        for ln in logical_lines:
            wrapped = wrap_line(c, ln, font, size, width)
            all_phys.extend(wrapped if wrapped else [""])

    c.setFont(font, size)
    c.setFillColor(RED)
    y_top_cursor = ytop_start + leading * 0.85
    for i, ln in enumerate(all_phys):
        y_rl = topY(y_top_cursor)
        if align == "left":
            c.drawString(x0, y_rl, ln)
        elif align == "center":
            c.drawCentredString((x0 + x1) / 2.0, y_rl, ln)
        y_top_cursor += leading
    return size

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import re, math
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from reportlab.lib.colors import Color
from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics
from reportlab.pdfbase.ttfonts import TTFont
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("DejaVu", "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf"))
pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("DejaVu-Bold", "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf"))

HEADER_RED = Color(0.55, 0.0, 0.0)
BODY_RED   = Color(0.75, 0.0, 0.0)
PAGE_W = 595.28003
PAGE_H = 841.89001

SRC_PDF = "/home/pop-os/Downloads/Form 4 Math Holiday PP1.pdf"
SCRATCH = "/tmp/claude-1000/-home-pop-os/15e4b6c9-9ae5-42ee-971c-ee3ad5f6dc18/scratchpad"
OUT_OVERLAY = SCRATCH + "/overlay2.pdf"
OUT_FINAL = SCRATCH + "/Form 4 Math Holiday PP1 - ANSWERED.pdf"

def topY(y_top):
    return PAGE_H - y_top

# ============================================================
# RICH TEXT ENGINE:  \f{num}{den} -> stacked fraction
#                    \x{exp}      -> superscript
# ============================================================
TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r'\\f\{([^}]*)\}\{([^}]*)\}|\\x\{([^}]*)\}')

FRAC_SCALE = 0.78
FRAC_PAD_FACTOR = 0.22
FRAC_BAR_RISE_FACTOR = 0.32
SUP_SCALE = 0.62
SUP_RISE_FACTOR = 0.40

def parse_rich(s):
    runs = []
    pos = 0
    for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(s):
        if m.start() > pos:
            runs.append(('t', s[pos:m.start()]))
        if m.group(1) is not None:
            runs.append(('f', m.group(1), m.group(2)))
        else:
            runs.append(('x', m.group(3)))
        pos = m.end()
    if pos < len(s):
        runs.append(('t', s[pos:]))
    return runs

def rich_width(runs, font, size):
    w = 0.0
    for r in runs:
        if r[0] == 't':
            w += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, size)
        elif r[0] == 'x':
            w += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, size * SUP_SCALE) + size * 0.06
        elif r[0] == 'f':
            nf = size * FRAC_SCALE
            nw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, nf)
            dw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[2], font, nf)
            fw = max(nw, dw) + 2 * size * FRAC_PAD_FACTOR
            w += fw
    return w

def rich_metrics(runs, size):
    has_f = any(r[0] == 'f' for r in runs)
    has_x = any(r[0] == 'x' for r in runs)
    if has_f:
        nf = size * FRAC_SCALE
        ascent = size * FRAC_BAR_RISE_FACTOR + nf * 0.95
        descent = nf * 0.95
        ascent = max(ascent, size * 0.80)
        descent = max(descent, size * 0.24)
    elif has_x:
        ascent = size * 0.80 + size * SUP_SCALE * 0.60
        descent = size * 0.24
    else:
        ascent = size * 0.80
        descent = size * 0.24
    return ascent, descent

def draw_rich_runs(c, x, y_baseline, runs, font, size, color):
    c.setFillColor(color)
    cx = x
    for r in runs:
        if r[0] == 't':
            c.setFont(font, size)
            c.drawString(cx, y_baseline, r[1])
            cx += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, size)
        elif r[0] == 'x':
            sf = size * SUP_SCALE
            c.setFont(font, sf)
            c.drawString(cx, y_baseline + size * SUP_RISE_FACTOR, r[1])
            cx += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, sf) + size * 0.06
        elif r[0] == 'f':
            nf = size * FRAC_SCALE
            nw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, nf)
            dw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[2], font, nf)
            fw = max(nw, dw)
            pad = size * FRAC_PAD_FACTOR
            barY = y_baseline + size * FRAC_BAR_RISE_FACTOR
            c.setFont(font, nf)
            c.drawCentredString(cx + pad + fw / 2.0, barY + nf * 0.20, r[1])
            c.setLineWidth(max(0.5, size * 0.045))
            c.line(cx + pad - 1, barY, cx + pad + fw + 1, barY)
            c.drawCentredString(cx + pad + fw / 2.0, barY - nf * 0.95, r[2])
            cx += fw + 2 * pad

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import re, math
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from reportlab.lib.colors import Color
from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics
from reportlab.pdfbase.ttfonts import TTFont
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter

pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("DejaVu", "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf"))
pdfmetrics.registerFont(TTFont("DejaVu-Bold", "/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf"))

HEADER_RED = Color(0.55, 0.0, 0.0)
BODY_RED   = Color(0.75, 0.0, 0.0)
PAGE_W = 595.28003
PAGE_H = 841.89001

SRC_PDF = "/home/pop-os/Downloads/Form 4 Math Holiday PP1.pdf"
SCRATCH = "/tmp/claude-1000/-home-pop-os/15e4b6c9-9ae5-42ee-971c-ee3ad5f6dc18/scratchpad"
OUT_OVERLAY = SCRATCH + "/overlay2.pdf"
OUT_FINAL = SCRATCH + "/Form 4 Math Holiday PP1 - ANSWERED.pdf"

def topY(y_top):
    return PAGE_H - y_top

# ============================================================
# RICH TEXT ENGINE:  \f{num}{den} -> stacked fraction
#                    \x{exp}      -> superscript
# ============================================================
TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r'\\f\{([^}]*)\}\{([^}]*)\}|\\x\{([^}]*)\}')

FRAC_SCALE = 0.78
FRAC_PAD_FACTOR = 0.22
FRAC_BAR_RISE_FACTOR = 0.32
SUP_SCALE = 0.62
SUP_RISE_FACTOR = 0.40

def parse_rich(s):
    runs = []
    pos = 0
    for m in TOKEN_RE.finditer(s):
        if m.start() > pos:
            runs.append(('t', s[pos:m.start()]))
        if m.group(1) is not None:
            runs.append(('f', m.group(1), m.group(2)))
        else:
            runs.append(('x', m.group(3)))
        pos = m.end()
    if pos < len(s):
        runs.append(('t', s[pos:]))
    return runs

def rich_width(runs, font, size):
    w = 0.0
    for r in runs:
        if r[0] == 't':
            w += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, size)
        elif r[0] == 'x':
            w += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, size * SUP_SCALE) + size * 0.06
        elif r[0] == 'f':
            nf = size * FRAC_SCALE
            nw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, nf)
            dw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[2], font, nf)
            fw = max(nw, dw) + 2 * size * FRAC_PAD_FACTOR
            w += fw
    return w

def rich_metrics(runs, size):
    has_f = any(r[0] == 'f' for r in runs)
    has_x = any(r[0] == 'x' for r in runs)
    if has_f:
        nf = size * FRAC_SCALE
        ascent = size * FRAC_BAR_RISE_FACTOR + nf * 0.95
        descent = nf * 0.95
        ascent = max(ascent, size * 0.80)
        descent = max(descent, size * 0.24)
    elif has_x:
        ascent = size * 0.80 + size * SUP_SCALE * 0.60
        descent = size * 0.24
    else:
        ascent = size * 0.80
        descent = size * 0.24
    return ascent, descent

def draw_rich_runs(c, x, y_baseline, runs, font, size, color):
    c.setFillColor(color)
    cx = x
    for r in runs:
        if r[0] == 't':
            c.setFont(font, size)
            c.drawString(cx, y_baseline, r[1])
            cx += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, size)
        elif r[0] == 'x':
            sf = size * SUP_SCALE
            c.setFont(font, sf)
            c.drawString(cx, y_baseline + size * SUP_RISE_FACTOR, r[1])
            cx += pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, sf) + size * 0.06
        elif r[0] == 'f':
            nf = size * FRAC_SCALE
            nw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[1], font, nf)
            dw = pdfmetrics.stringWidth(r[2], font, nf)
            fw = max(nw, dw)
            pad = size * FRAC_PAD_FACTOR
            barY = y_baseline + size * FRAC_BAR_RISE_FACTOR
            c.setFont(font, nf)
            c.drawCentredString(cx + pad + fw / 2.0, barY + nf * 0.20, r[1])
            c.setLineWidth(max(0.5, size * 0.045))
            c.line(cx + pad - 1, barY, cx + pad + fw + 1, barY)
            c.drawCentredString(cx + pad + fw / 2.0, barY - nf * 0.95, r[2])
            cx += fw + 2 * pad
    return cx - x

def wrap_rich_line(text, font, size, max_width):
    words = text.split(' ')
    lines = []
    cur = []
    for w in words:
        trial = cur + [w]
        s = ' '.join(trial)
        if rich_width(parse_rich(s), font, size) <= max_width or not cur:
            cur = trial
        else:
            lines.append(' '.join(cur))
            cur = [w]
    if cur:
        lines.append(' '.join(cur))
    return lines

def fit_and_draw(c, x0, x1, ytop_start, ytop_end, logical_lines,
                  max_size=12.5, min_size=6.0, color=BODY_RED, font="DejaVu"):
    width = x1 - x0
    height = ytop_end - ytop_start
    if height <= 0 or not logical_lines:
        return 0
    size = max_size
    chosen = None
    while size >= min_size:
        phys = []
        for ln in logical_lines:
            wrapped = wrap_rich_line(ln, font, size, width)
            phys.extend(wrapped if wrapped else [""])
        mets = [rich_metrics(parse_rich(pl), size) for pl in phys]
        gap = size * 0.22
        tight_h = sum(a + d for a, d in mets) + gap * max(0, len(phys) - 1)
        if tight_h <= height:
            chosen = (size, phys, mets, gap, tight_h)
            break
        size -= 0.5
    if chosen is None:
        size = min_size
        phys = []
        for ln in logical_lines:
            wrapped = wrap_rich_line(ln, font, size, width)
            phys.extend(wrapped if wrapped else [""])
        mets = [rich_metrics(parse_rich(pl), size) for pl in phys]
        gap = size * 0.15
        tight_h = sum(a + d for a, d in mets) + gap * max(0, len(phys) - 1)
        chosen = (size, phys, mets, gap, tight_h)

    size, phys, mets, gap, tight_h = chosen
    n = len(phys)
    slack = max(0.0, height - tight_h)
    extra_gap = 0.0
    top_margin = 0.0
    if slack > 0:
        if n > 1:
            max_extra_gap = size * 0.60
            extra_gap = min(max_extra_gap, (slack / (n - 1)) * 0.75)
        block_h = tight_h + extra_gap * max(0, n - 1)
        top_margin = max(0.0, (height - block_h) / 2.0)
        top_margin = min(top_margin, max(0.0, height - block_h))

    y_cursor = ytop_start + top_margin
    for i, (pl, (a, d)) in enumerate(zip(phys, mets)):
        y_cursor += a
        draw_rich_runs(c, x0, topY(y_cursor), parse_rich(pl), font, size, color)
        y_cursor += d
        if i < n - 1:
            y_cursor += gap + extra_gap
    return size

def draw_header(c, x0, x1, ytop_start, ytop_end, header_text, size=9.3):
    width = x1 - x0
    lines = wrap_rich_line(header_text, "DejaVu-Bold", size, width)
    y_cursor = ytop_start
    for pl in lines:
        runs = parse_rich(pl)
        a, d = rich_metrics(runs, size)
        y_cursor += a
        draw_rich_runs(c, x0, topY(y_cursor), runs, "DejaVu-Bold", size, HEADER_RED)
        y_cursor += d + size * 0.12
    c.setStrokeColor(HEADER_RED)
    c.setLineWidth(0.7)
    rule_y = topY(y_cursor + 1.5)
    c.line(x0, rule_y, x0 + min(width, 210), rule_y)
    return min(ytop_end, y_cursor + 6.0)

    y_rl = topY(y_mid_top)
    c.setStrokeColor(BODY_RED); c.setFillColor(BODY_RED); c.setLineWidth(1.1)
    lo, hi = -3, 6
    usable_w = (x1 - x0) - 20
    step = usable_w / (hi - lo)
    def X(v): return x0 + 10 + (v - lo) * step
    c.line(X(lo) - 6, y_rl, X(hi) + 10, y_rl)
    ax = X(hi) + 10
    c.line(ax, y_rl, ax - 6, y_rl + 3)
    c.line(ax, y_rl, ax - 6, y_rl - 3)
    c.setFont("DejaVu", 7.5)
    for v in range(lo, hi + 1):
        xx = X(v)
        c.line(xx, y_rl - 3, xx, y_rl + 3)
        c.drawCentredString(xx, y_rl - 13, str(v))
    r = 3.2
    c.circle(X(1), y_rl, r, stroke=1, fill=1)
    c.setLineWidth(2.2)
    c.line(X(1), y_rl, X(hi), y_rl)
    c.setFont("DejaVu", 7.5)
    c.drawCentredString((X(1) + X(hi)) / 2.0, y_rl + 9, "x ≥ 1")

def draw_sketch_18biii(c, x0, x1, ytop_start, ytop_end):
    xs = [i / 20.0 for i in range(-70, 26)]
    pts = [(x, (1.0 / 3.0) * x**3 + x**2) for x in xs]
    ymin = min(p[1] for p in pts); ymax = max(p[1] for p in pts)
    xmin = min(p[0] for p in pts); xmax = max(p[0] for p in pts)
    W = x1 - x0 - 20
    H = (ytop_end - ytop_start) - 20
    sx = W / (xmax - xmin)
    sy = H / (ymax - ymin)
    ox = x0 + 12 - xmin * sx

    def X(xv): return ox + xv * sx
    def Ytop(yv): return (ytop_start + 12) + (ymax - yv) * sy

    c.setStrokeColor(BODY_RED); c.setFillColor(BODY_RED); c.setLineWidth(0.9)
    if xmin <= 0 <= xmax:
        c.line(X(0), topY(Ytop(ymax)), X(0), topY(Ytop(ymin)))
    if ymin <= 0 <= ymax:
        c.line(X(xmin), topY(Ytop(0)), X(xmax), topY(Ytop(0)))
    c.setLineWidth(1.3)
    path = c.beginPath()
    path.moveTo(X(pts[0][0]), topY(Ytop(pts[0][1])))
    for (xv, yv) in pts[1:]:
        path.lineTo(X(xv), topY(Ytop(yv)))
    c.drawPath(path, stroke=1, fill=0)
    for (xv, yv, lbl) in [(-2, 4/3.0, "max"), (0, 0, "min")]:

    c.drawString(X(-2) - 10, topY(Ytop(4/3.0)) + 4, "(-2,4/3)")
    c.drawString(X(0) + 2, topY(Ytop(0)) - 8, "(0,0)")

    R = (59.3022, 4.2337)
    S = (40.378, -14.696)
    pts = {"P": P, "Q": Q, "R": R, "S": S}
    xs = [p[0] for p in pts.values()]; ys = [p[1] for p in pts.values()]
    xr = max(xs) - min(xs); yr = max(ys) - min(ys)
    margin = 22
    W = (x1 - x0) - 2 * margin
    H = (ytop_end - ytop_start) - 2 * margin
    scale = min(W / xr, H / yr)
    ox = x0 + margin - min(xs) * scale
    oytop = ytop_start + margin

    def X(km_x): return ox + km_x * scale
    def Ytop(km_y): return oytop + (max(ys) - km_y) * scale

    c.setStrokeColor(BODY_RED); c.setFillColor(BODY_RED); c.setLineWidth(1.0)
    order = ["P", "Q", "R", "S", "P"]
    path = c.beginPath()
    first = pts[order[0]]
    path.moveTo(X(first[0]), topY(Ytop(first[1])))
    for k in order[1:]:
        p = pts[k]
        path.lineTo(X(p[0]), topY(Ytop(p[1])))
    c.drawPath(path, stroke=1, fill=0)

    c.setFont("DejaVu-Bold", 8)
    for k, p in pts.items():
        px, py = X(p[0]), topY(Ytop(p[1]))
        c.circle(px, py, 1.6, stroke=1, fill=1)
        dx, dy = (4, 4) if k != "S" else (4, -10)
        c.drawString(px + dx, py + dy, k)

    px, py = X(P[0]), topY(Ytop(P[1]))
    c.setLineWidth(0.8)
    c.line(px, py, px, py + 20)
    c.line(px, py + 20, px - 2.5, py + 15)
    c.line(px, py + 20, px + 2.5, py + 15)
    c.setFont("DejaVu", 6)
    c.drawCentredString(px, py + 22, "N")

    bar_len = 10 * scale
    bx0 = x0 + margin
    by = topY(ytop_end - 4)
    c.setLineWidth(1.0)
    c.line(bx0, by, bx0 + bar_len, by)

            c.drawCentredString(X(xv), Yrl(0) - 12, str(xv))
    for yv in range(-2, 11, 2):
        c.line(X(0) - 3, Yrl(yv), X(0) + 3, Yrl(yv))
        if yv != 0:
            c.drawString(X(0) + 5, Yrl(yv) - 3, str(yv))
    c.drawString(X(3.3) - 8, Yrl(0) + 6, "x")
    c.drawString(X(0) + 6, Yrl(10.4) - 8, "y")

    c.setLineWidth(1.4)
    xs = [-3 + i * 0.05 for i in range(0, 121)]
    path = c.beginPath()
    x0v = xs[0]; path.moveTo(X(x0v), Yrl(x0v**2 - x0v - 2))
    for xv in xs[1:]:
        path.lineTo(X(xv), Yrl(xv**2 - xv - 2))
    c.drawPath(path, stroke=1, fill=0)

    c.setLineWidth(1.1)
    c.setDash(4, 3)
    c.line(X(-3), Yrl(5), X(3), Yrl(-1))
    c.setDash()

    c.setFont("DejaVu", 6.5)
    table_pts = [(-3, 10), (-2, 4), (-1, 0), (0, -2), (1, -2), (2, 0), (3, 4)]
    for (xv, yv) in table_pts:
        c.circle(X(xv), Yrl(yv), 1.6, stroke=1, fill=1)

    for (xv, yv, lbl) in [(-2, 4, "(-2,4)"), (2, 0, "(2,0)"), (0.5, -2.25, "min(0.5,-2.25)")]:
        c.circle(X(xv), Yrl(yv), 2.2, stroke=1, fill=1)
        c.drawString(X(xv) + 4, Yrl(yv) + 3, lbl)

def main():
    c = canvas.Canvas(OUT_OVERLAY, pagesize=(PAGE_W, PAGE_H))
    reader = PdfReader(SRC_PDF)
    n_pages = len(reader.pages)

    for pnum in range(1, n_pages + 1):
        zones = Z.get(pnum, {})
        for qid, (x0, x1, y0, y1) in zones.items():
            if qid in ("Q9NL", "Q18biii", "Q19a"):
                continue
            lines = ANSWERS.get(qid)
            if not lines:
                continue
            zy0 = y0
            if qid in HEADERS:
                zy0 = draw_header(c, x0, x1, y0, y1, HEADERS[qid])
            fit_and_draw(c, x0, x1, zy0, y1, lines)

        if pnum == 5:
            zx0, zx1, zy0, zy1 = Z[5]["Q9NL"]
            draw_number_line(c, zx0, zx1, zy0, zy1)
        if pnum == 10:
            zx0, zx1, zy0, zy1 = Z[10]["Q18biii"]
            draw_sketch_18biii(c, zx0, zx1, zy0, zy1)
            zx0, zx1, zy0, zy1 = Z[10]["Q19a"]
            draw_bearing_diagram(c, zx0, zx1, zy0, zy1)
        if pnum == 15:
            fill_table23(c)
        if pnum == 16:
            draw_graph23(c)

        c.showPage()

    c.save()
    print("Overlay written:", OUT_OVERLAY)

    base = PdfReader(SRC_PDF)
    overlay = PdfReader(OUT_OVERLAY)
    writer = PdfWriter()
    for i, page in enumerate(base.pages):
        if i < len(overlay.pages):
            page.merge_page(overlay.pages[i])
        writer.add_page(page)
    with open(OUT_FINAL, "wb") as f:
        writer.write(f)
    print("Final answered PDF written:", OUT_FINAL)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---
# The Goodness of God
## A Teaching by Mary Wamuyu
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Kesha — Covenant Month of Healings
**Late March – Early April 2026**

---

> *"Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*
> — Hosea 10:12 (NKJV)

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

I want us to go to this verse we have been having for this kesha — Hosea 10:12. You know, you may have one hour to preach and read your notes, and then in the thirtieth minute you will have to ask the Holy Spirit to help you. Let's read it together.

*"Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap in mercy; break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord, till He comes and rains righteousness on you."*

I want to bring an emphasis on "break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the Lord." If you remember the last meeting we had here, our father was teaching, and he spoke a lot about — let me say it in general — **restoration**. He spoke about how, if you had lost fellowship with the Holy Spirit, there was a restoration that day. Because that is the only way that fallow ground can be broken. Only by the Spirit of God.

That is why there has been such a great emphasis lately on the love of God. Because when you have the understanding of that love, you are conscious of the Holy Spirit, and it is by that Holy Spirit that this fallow ground breaks. And once it breaks, you are now able to seek the Lord.

I need you to be very attentive tonight. Because today, God is going to heal your heart.

---

## Called Into Communion, Not Just Service

If there has been an emphasis for any believer, one thing you should understand is this: as much as you are called, and God calls you for the people — **He first calls you for Himself.** God is pleased with your service, but that is not His first agenda in your life. His first agenda is to have communion with Him.

That's why I don't like to call it religion. It calls us to a place of relationship. We are not "like God, and then us, and then there is that." We are a people that God dwells in. That makes the whole difference. Because when the Bible says "seek Him," it is actually from within, from a place of fellowship — not from a place of "that is God, here I am," and then you go and come back.

That's why we don't measure our righteousness by our actions. **It's not about the doing. It's about the becoming.**

> *"The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly."*
> — John 10:10 (NKJV)

When He says there is a life He has given us, and a more abundant one, it is because it's a call to fully live like Him. We are an expression of the glory of God.

> *"I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me; and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me."*
> — Galatians 2:20 (NKJV)

We are entering the month of April — our covenant month of healings. As we were closing up March, God laid a very high emphasis on my heart: what He is going to heal us from is **lack of understanding.** Me and you too, both. He's speaking to us through me — to us. Because we have been at a place where you are looking at things, and you cannot trace the love of God in them. And today, I want you to see the love of God in them. The Lord is going to open your eyes.

---

## The Word of God Is Alive, and It Must Grow

When you're reading the Bible, you're not just gaining knowledge — you are being called into a person. Jesus is the Word. The Word made flesh.

> *"And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth."*
> — John 1:14 (NKJV)

So when you read the Word of God, you are not just gaining knowledge; you are being made into Christ. You're being formed to become one with Him.

But how many times have you read the Word of God and thought, that's for my neighbor — that will work for them, but I look at my life and it's not making sense? Brethren, it does not have to make sense. The Bible says that Word is living and active. So anytime the Word of God is introduced to a situation, it brings life.

It's like pouring water on a seed that has been planted. That seed must germinate. It has received the necessary requirement — light, water, all of it. **That seed has no option. It must grow.** That is the Word of God for you. When that situation receives the Word of God, it must grow. There is nothing — the Bible says all things shall pass away. What will remain? The Word. Why? Because it's unchangeable.

---

## Nothing Can Separate You From His Love

Romans 8 says God is love. It is not a character trait. It is His Person. He *is* love. Nothing can take love away from God. There is only one thing He hates — He hates sin. But Him and love cannot be separated.

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38–39 (NKJV)

It has tried to look at every single thing in the sphere of life, until it finishes with "any other created thing" — in case it left anything somewhere, that it be covered there too. Meaning **nothing.** And I repeat: nothing can separate you from the love of God.

Now, this love of God that you cannot be separated from — it is *in Christ Jesus.* When you get born again, where are you? In Christ Jesus. And in Christ Jesus is a blessed soul. There is something in Christ Jesus called the love of God, and now that you are there, you must behold that love. It is there. And nothing can pick you out and prick you out of that place.

That means God continually loves you. There is no place where He is saying, "Because of the things you have done, I need a break from you." The Bible says:

> *"Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness."*
> — Lamentations 3:22–23 (NKJV)

Every morning you wake up, God gives you a blank page. He is not shocked by you. The way our father tells us — you don't shock God. You come to Him with something you've done, and He already saw it. He is not surprised. So you come with a blank page. Every morning. "My son, I love you. Before you show me your drama — take the blank page."

But we know very well the book of Romans says that is not a support for us to continually sin. That has not given you a key to now do whatever you wish.

---

## When It Feels Like His Love Has Left

A question arises. Then why do you, at certain times, feel like God has left? Like this love has left you?

This might come from a place of **condemnation.** You have done a thing, and you look at yourself and think there is no way this love can be flowing toward me anymore. Or it might be **guilt** — guilt has consumed you to a point you cannot tell if this love is with you. Another thing is **pain.** You have gone through something until you feel like this boat has already sunk, and you are here alone. And there is **focusing on yourself** — you look at yourself and see so much inability. "What can I? What can I? Everything is cannot, cannot, cannot."

Have you been in those places? But I have come to remind you today: **nothing can separate you from that love of God that is in Christ Jesus.**

The Bible says we walk by faith and not by sight. Condemnation is a feeling. Pain is a feeling. Guilt is a feeling. That is a place of walking by sight — by what you can see, and I don't just mean eyes, I mean feelings too. But the Bible calls you, as a believer, to a place of living by faith and not by sight.

> *"For we walk by faith, not by sight."*
> — 2 Corinthians 5:7 (NKJV)

There is something no one will ever do for you in this walk. We will love you, pray for you, cast out demons for you — but walking by faith, we will not do it for you. You will be in a cycle time and again, because there is a miracle you are expecting, yet the only miracle you actually need at that point is to walk by faith.

Is it easy? No. It is a point where it will lead you to even crawl. You will pull yourself. But there is a reward. And God will not lower His principles for you. He will not say, "Since your life looks like this, let's just allow you to walk by sight a little." There is no shortcut. It will be painful, but there is no shortcut. You must walk by faith.

That's where you take the Word of God and hide it in your heart to live by it — I *choose* to walk by faith. Because if you choose to walk by sight instead, you will mark time. You will have to repeat that class. And when the Bible says walk by faith, it says so.

---

## Understanding the Character of God

Another thing that will help you stand is being able to understand the character of God. This is a place we fail terribly as believers — because the purpose of you becoming a believer is not, per se, to do things. It is to *become.*

We have gotten to a place where we leave our man of God at some award, expecting him to come and pray and prophesy over us. I have a covering — that is true, it's not a lie. But he will never leave your life for you. He cannot. As much as you have spiritual authority over you, *you* are responsible for your life. As much as your father loves you, he will pray for you, prophesy over you, speak over your life — but he will never sit down and cultivate a personal relationship with God on your behalf.

If you don't have that relationship yourself, you don't have counsel with the Holy Spirit. You cannot have a discussion. So if I come and tell you, "If someone does A, B, C, D, God will punish them," and you lack that truth for yourself, you will take that word and run with it — because there is a deficiency in your own relationship with the Holy Spirit. And you will walk in a lie for the rest of your life, until you choose to seek Him while He may be found.

Tonight, I want us to focus on one thing: **the goodness of God.** Tell your neighbor — the goodness of God.

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

Anytime someone tells you God is good, and all the time — you know how we finish that. It's become a slogan, like a greeting. "How are you?" "I'm fine." "God is good, all the time — and all the time, God is good." **That is His nature.** The goodness of God is not determined by your experiences. He is inseparable from His goodness. God *is* good.

I want us to understand what it means when we say God is good.

### 1. God Has No Moral Weakness

**God cannot use His power against you.** He cannot use His authority to take from you.

Do you remember the story of Naboth? In the book of Kings, there is a man named Naboth, and he had a vineyard.

> *"But Naboth said to Ahab, 'The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!'"*
> — 1 Kings 21:3 (NKJV)

Ahab looked at that vineyard and wanted it, but Naboth refused — because it was the inheritance of his fathers. And where did that man end up? Dead. Because of his vineyard. But look at what I am telling you: **that is not how God operates.** God does not have moral weakness. God cannot grab your land just because He has the authority to do so.

There was a time in my life I felt like I was telling God, "It's fine, You can do whatever You want with me" — like resigning myself, because I felt like God was using His power on me since I could not do anything about it. But God does not have moral weakness. God does not put you at a disadvantage just because "I am God, and you are Eunice." God is not a politician looking for your vote so He can sit on the throne. Did you vote for Him? Will you now remove Him?

> *"And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist."*
> — Colossians 1:17 (NKJV)

Why would you think God, in His might, would contemplate taking something from you just because He has the ability to? He does not have moral weakness. He is not trying to prove a point by taking something from you.

### 2. God Is Kind

What is kindness? If this phone belonged to me, and I decided to give it to you, I have shown you kindness — because I have done it *for* you, and it was not something you were owed, not something you had paid for, not even something you were expecting.

Now, when the Bible says God is good, and one part of that is that God is kind, it means **the intention of God is to do things unto you.** He is thinking of good things toward you — because you cannot show someone kindness by taking things from them. Now God is kind. He does everything for you.

Someone will ask: what about the situations where there is pain? In whatever situation, **God cannot deny Himself.** The Bible has called Him good — so even there, He is showing you kindness. What you ought to do is see it in His light.

Why? Because it's unchangeable.

---

## Nothing Can Separate You From His Love

Romans 8 says God is love. It is not a character trait. It is His Person. He *is* love. Nothing can take love away from God. There is only one thing He hates — He hates sin. But Him and love cannot be separated.

> *"For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord."*
> — Romans 8:38–39 (NKJV)

It has tried to look at every single thing in the sphere of life, until it finishes with "any other created thing" — in case it left anything somewhere, that it be covered there too. Meaning **nothing.** And I repeat: nothing can separate you from the love of God.

Now, this love of God that you cannot be separated from — it is *in Christ Jesus.* When you get born again, where are you? In Christ Jesus. And in Christ Jesus is a blessed soul. There is something in Christ Jesus called the love of God, and now that you are there, you must behold that love. It is there. And nothing can pick you out and prick you out of that place.

That means God continually loves you. There is no place where He is saying, "Because of the things you have done, I need a break from you." The Bible says:

> *"Through the LORD's mercies we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not. They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness."*
> — Lamentations 3:22–23 (NKJV)

Every morning you wake up, God gives you a blank page. He is not shocked by you. The way our father tells us — you don't shock God. You come to Him with something you've done, and He already saw it. He is not surprised. So you come with a blank page. Every morning. "My son, I love you. Before you show me your drama — take the blank page."

But we know very well the book of Romans says that is not a support for us to continually sin. That has not given you a key to now do whatever you wish.

---

## When It Feels Like His Love Has Left

A question arises. Then why do you, at certain times, feel like God has left? Like this love has left you?

This might come from a place of **condemnation.** You have done a thing, and you look at yourself and think there is no way this love can be flowing toward me anymore. Or it might be **guilt** — guilt has consumed you to a point you cannot tell if this love is with you. Another thing is **pain.** You have gone through something until you feel like this boat has already sunk, and you are here alone. And there is **focusing on yourself** — you look at yourself and see so much inability. "What can I? What can I? Everything is cannot, cannot, cannot."

Have you been in those places? But I have come to remind you today: **nothing can separate you from that love of God that is in Christ Jesus.**

The Bible says we walk by faith and not by sight. Condemnation is a feeling. Pain is a feeling. Guilt is a feeling. That is a place of walking by sight — by what you can see, and I don't just mean eyes, I mean feelings too. But the Bible calls you, as a believer, to a place of living by faith and not by sight.

> *"For we walk by faith, not by sight."*
> — 2 Corinthians 5:7 (NKJV)

There is something no one will ever do for you in this walk. We will love you, pray for you, cast out demons for you — but walking by faith, we will not do it for you. You will be in a cycle time and again, because there is a miracle you are expecting, yet the only miracle you actually need at that point is to walk by faith.

Is it easy? No. It is a point where it will lead you to even crawl. You will pull yourself. But there is a reward. And God will not lower His principles for you. He will not say, "Since your life looks like this, let's just allow you to walk by sight a little." There is no shortcut. It will be painful, but there is no shortcut. You must walk by faith.

That's where you take the Word of God and hide it in your heart to live by it — I *choose* to walk by faith. Because if you choose to walk by sight instead, you will mark time. You will have to repeat that class. And when the Bible says walk by faith, it says so.

---

## Understanding the Character of God

Another thing that will help you stand is being able to understand the character of God. This is a place we fail terribly as believers — because the purpose of you becoming a believer is not, per se, to do things. It is to *become.*

We have gotten to a place where we leave our man of God at some award, expecting him to come and pray and prophesy over us. I have a covering — that is true, it's not a lie. But he will never leave your life for you. He cannot. As much as you have spiritual authority over you, *you* are responsible for your life. As much as your father loves you, he will pray for you, prophesy over you, speak over your life — but he will never sit down and cultivate a personal relationship with God on your behalf.

If you don't have that relationship yourself, you don't have counsel with the Holy Spirit. You cannot have a discussion. So if I come and tell you, "If someone does A, B, C, D, God will punish them," and you lack that truth for yourself, you will take that word and run with it — because there is a deficiency in your own relationship with the Holy Spirit. And you will walk in a lie for the rest of your life, until you choose to seek Him while He may be found.

Tonight, I want us to focus on one thing: **the goodness of God.** Tell your neighbor — the goodness of God.

> *"Praise the LORD! Oh, give thanks to the LORD, for He is good! For His mercy endures forever."*
> — Psalm 106:1 (NKJV)

Anytime someone tells you God is good, and all the time — you know how we finish that. It's become a slogan, like a greeting. "How are you?" "I'm fine." "God is good, all the time — and all the time, God is good." **That is His nature.** The goodness of God is not determined by your experiences. He is inseparable from His goodness. God *is* good.

I want us to understand what it means when we say God is good.

### 1. God Has No Moral Weakness

**God cannot use His power against you.** He cannot use His authority to take from you.

Do you remember the story of Naboth? In the book of Kings, there is a man named Naboth, and he had a vineyard.

> *"But Naboth said to Ahab, 'The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!'"*
> — 1 Kings 21:3 (NKJV)

Ahab looked at that vineyard and wanted it, but Naboth refused — because it was the inheritance of his fathers. And where did that man end up? Dead. Because of his vineyard. But look at what I am telling you: **that is not how God operates.** God does not have moral weakness. God cannot grab your land just because He has the authority to do so.

There was a time in my life I felt like I was telling God, "It's fine, You can do whatever You want with me" — like resigning myself, because I felt like God was using His power on me since I could not do anything about it. But God does not have moral weakness. God does not put you at a disadvantage just because "I am God, and you are Eunice." God is not a politician looking for your vote so He can sit on the throne. Did you vote for Him? Will you now remove Him?

> *"And He is before all things, and in Him all things consist."*
> — Colossians 1:17 (NKJV)

Why would you think God, in His might, would contemplate taking something from you just because He has the ability to? He does not have moral weakness. He is not trying to prove a point by taking something from you.

### 2. God Is Kind

What is kindness? If this phone belonged to me, and I decided to give it to you, I have shown you kindness — because I have done it *for* you, and it was not something you were owed, not something you had paid for, not even something you were expecting.

Now, when the Bible says God is good, and one part of that is that God is kind, it means **the intention of God is to do things unto you.** He is thinking of good things toward you — because you cannot show someone kindness by taking things from them. Now God is kind. He does everything for you.

Someone will ask: what about the situations where there is pain? In whatever situation, **God cannot deny Himself.** The Bible has called Him good — so even there, He is showing you kindness. What you ought to do is see it in His light.

> *"Now Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him."*
> — Genesis 21:5 (NKJV)

That is twenty-five years. And you, if you haven't reached twenty-five years of waiting — Abraham waited twenty-five years for a son. Wouldn't you have started asking God, "Just give me this son so I can at least see grandchildren"? But what does the Bible say?

> *"By faith Sarah herself also received strength to conceive seed, and she bore a child when she was past the age, because she judged Him faithful who had promised."*
> — Hebrews 11:11 (NKJV)

Abraham woke up year after year, wishing people well through twenty-five years — while other men his age were already seeing grandchildren — and he was still waiting for his firstborn. And then, as if that was not enough, after twenty-five years, when the boy had come and been raised, and Abraham had finally seen the promise, there is *still* something else God asked of him.

That's how we have nullified some things — because there is a pattern we've created for how God "should" work. But God is not boxed. He will not fit your sack. The Bible says we know in part. So what makes you think you already have it figured out how God is going to do it? Stop boxing Him. Allow Him to be God.

> *"For the vision is yet for an appointed time; but at the end it will speak, and it will not lie. Though it tarries, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry."*
> — Habakkuk 2:3 (NKJV)

That is an assurance. Because it is the Word of God, it is not from a motivational book — it is God saying, "It may take long, but it will come to pass." Child of God, I don't care how long it has taken. It shall surely come to pass.

---

## Refuse to Glorify Pain

We have a tendency, as believers, to feel like having troubles is humility. "Even I have struggled to pray and read the Word — even me, not just you." We laugh, but that's pride landing on us in a different shape. We have glorified pain. We have glorified failure. We have glorified a lack of excellence just so we can fit in with everyone else.

**Refuse that, in the name of Jesus.** You carry God. You cannot be anything less. So don't try to shrink yourself to fit in. If you're able to do something, help the person who is not able. Stop soothing each other's egos instead of helping each other grow — you know it's not the truth, and yet you let them go home still carrying it. Why don't you help them instead?

---

## The Closing Declarations

*Will you walk in what God has called you to be?* — **Yes.**
*Will you stand in the promises of God upon your life?* — **Yes.**
*Do you promise to do that?* — **Yes.**

> *"God is changing your story. I receive."*

You have been here for a whole three months — you cannot go back and continue walking in the old ways.

> *"If the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed."*
> — John 8:36 (NKJV)

It is up to you to make that decision — to walk in alignment with the Word of God, to believe that He is faithful.

> *"If we are faithless, He remains faithful; He cannot deny Himself."*
> — 2 Timothy 2:13 (NKJV)

Even when you have given up on that situation, **God has not.** God has not given up on you, child of God. God is with you. You will not fail. Your banner has been lifted up high. You will not fail. **I receive.**

*As the congregation declared together:*

> *"I will walk in the truth of the Word of God."*

There is a lot of refreshing happening right now — that is what is going to happen to most people here, in the name of Jesus.

> *"That He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word."*
> — Ephesians 5:26 (NKJV)

*Let there be a washing.* A washing of the wounds you have carried for a very, very long time. Let there be a washing for the things you have trusted God for so long — you have not been forgotten.

> *"...there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother."*
> — Proverbs 18:24 (NKJV)

So close. So close. So close. The Bible has taught us — we reap in mercy as we sow in righteousness.

**You will have your harvest, in the name of Jesus. You will have your harvest, in the name of Jesus. I receive.**

*Open your mouth, Father, I thank You.*

1. **You are not called first for service — you are called first for communion.** It's not about the doing. It's about the becoming.
2. **The Word of God, once received, has no option but to grow** — like a seed given light and water.

=== skill.md ===
# Audio Series → Split → Transcribe → Compile Skill

## Purpose

Turn a folder of long raw audio/video recordings (a multi-part sermon/lecture/talk series,
meeting recordings, etc.) into one polished, chronologically-correct, voice-preserving
markdown document — reproducibly, end to end: **split** into manageable chunks, **transcribe**
each chunk via a speech-to-text API, **consolidate** chunks back into one transcript per
source recording, then **compile** all of it into a single publication-quality document using
an LLM with a specific, load-bearing prompt.

Built and verified on a real 5-part "Faith" sermon series (Pastor Charles Muchemi): 5 source
`.mp4` files (53–99 minutes each) → 17 stream-copy-split parts → 17 real transcriptions via
the Modulate STT API → 5 consolidated per-session transcripts → 1 compiled 6-session teaching
document with correct chronological reordering (the numbered parts were **not** taught in
1-2-3-4-5 order — the compile step had to figure that out from internal evidence).

---

## When to Use

Invoke when a request combines any of:
- "split this audio/video into chunks" + "transcribe it" — the mechanical first half.
- "turn these sermon/lecture/meeting recordings into one document" — the compile step.
- A series of recordings whose *file order* is known to not match the *actual teaching
  order* (very common with sermon series, recurring lecture series, multi-session
  workshops) — this skill's compile step exists specifically for that case.
- "don't leave anything out" + "make it read like [speaker] is talking to the reader" —
  the voice-preservation requirement this skill's prompt is tuned for.

Do NOT use for:
- A single short recording that doesn't need splitting — just transcribe it directly.
- Content where summarization (not full-fidelity compilation) is actually wanted — this
  skill is explicitly anti-summary; see the prompt's "do not leave out a thing."
- Transcription of copyrighted/third-party material without the rights to do so.

---

## Environment Reality (learned the hard way)

| Constraint | Detail | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **Filenames with spaces + unquoted bash loops** | `for p in $some_var` where `$some_var` holds space-containing paths silently word-splits — and can leave a stray `cat`/similar command with zero real arguments, which then **hangs reading stdin** instead of erroring. | Never iterate an unquoted variable of paths. Use bash arrays (`arr=("$dir"/*.ext)`) or `nullglob` + a `for f in "$dir"/*.ext` loop with the glob itself quoted-per-token, never `$(ls ...)` fed into an unquoted `for`. |
| **`ffmpeg -f segment -c copy` isn't frame-exact** | Requested 1740s (29min) segments came out as 1740.01–1740.03s in practice — it snaps to the nearest packet/keyframe boundary since there's no re-encode. | Expect ~tens-of-milliseconds drift, not exact cuts. Don't build downstream logic that assumes exact segment lengths. |
| **A binary named `brave`/`ffmpeg`/etc. "works" once, then silently no-ops** | Not applicable to `ffmpeg` specifically here, but the general lesson from this session: always verify a command actually ran (check its real exit code / process count / output file), don't trust that a prior successful invocation means the pattern is reliable every time. | For a batch job (17 files here), verify per-file (duration check, non-empty output) rather than trusting the loop completed cleanly just because it exited 0. |
| **The Modulate STT API is synchronous batch, not async/polling** | `POST /velma-2-stt-batch` blocks until the transcript is ready and returns it directly — no job-id + poll-status dance. | A ~4MB / 29-minute audio part took roughly 1-2 minutes per call in practice. For a full series (17 parts here) budget 20-30 minutes total, run it as a background task, don't block on it synchronously in a foreground call with a short timeout. |
| **Source files can arrive incrementally** | In the real run, `Faith 4.mp4` and `Faith 5.mp4` were dropped into the folder in separate later requests, well after 1-3 were already split/transcribed. | Every script here is written idempotent/incremental by design: `split-audio.sh` only touches files matching the naming pattern, `transcribe.py` skips any file that already has a non-empty transcript. Just re-run the same three commands on the whole folder each time new source files show up. |

---

## Required Inputs

| Input | How to obtain |
|---|---|
| Source recordings | Named `<PREFIX> <N>.<ext>` (e.g. `Faith 1.mp4`) — the scripts here rely on this exact naming to auto-discover files and derive output names. Rename first if they don't already follow it. |
| `ffmpeg` | `sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg` (also installs `ffprobe`, used to sanity-check durations) |
| A speech-to-text API + key | This skill is written against **Modulate** (`docs.modulate.ai`) — see §"Modulate API Reference" below for the exact contract. Swap `bin/transcribe.py`'s `API_URL`/request shape if using a different provider; the rest of the pipeline (split, consolidate, compile) is provider-agnostic. |
| `python3` + `requests` | `python3 -c "import requests"` to check; `pip install requests` (or your distro's equivalent) if missing. |
| (For the compile step) An LLM with file-attachment or Write-tool access | Either paste the filled-in prompt from `prompts/compile-teaching.md` into a chat with the transcripts attached, or hand an agent the transcripts + that file and ask it to follow the Structural Rulebook directly. |
| (Optional but valuable) Broader-context recordings | Full session/meeting recordings that cover the same material more broadly than the curated numbered parts — these help the compile step recover true chronological order. Not required, but noticeably improves the result if available. |

---

## Modulate API Reference (verified against the real docs and a real call)

- **Base URL:** `https://platform.modulate.ai/api`
- **Auth:** header `X-API-Key: <key>` (not `Authorization: Bearer`)
- **Endpoint used here:** `POST /velma-2-stt-batch` — multilingual, synchronous, speaker
  diarization available
- **Submission:** multipart form, field name `upload_file`
- **Supported formats:** `.aac .aiff .flac .mov .mp3 .mp4 .ogg .opus .wav .webm`
- **Limits:** 100MB max file size (`413` if exceeded), empty files rejected (`400`)
- **Response:** `{"text": "...", "duration_ms": N, "utterances": [{"utterance_uuid", "text",
  "start_ms", "duration_ms", "speaker", "language", ...}]}` — this skill's script only uses
  the top-level `text` field; `utterances` is there if you want per-speaker/per-timestamp
  breakdown later.
- **Faster alternative:** `/velma-2-stt-batch-english-vfast` — same shape, English-only,
  faster, no emotion/accent/deepfake signals. Swap `API_URL` in `bin/transcribe.py` if
  speed matters more than the multilingual model's extra signals.
- **API key handling:** store it at `~/.config/modulate/api_key`, `chmod 600`, **never**
  hardcode it in a script or commit it anywhere. Create it with:
  ```bash
  mkdir -p ~/.config/modulate
  umask 077
  printf '<your key>' > ~/.config/modulate/api_key
  chmod 600 ~/.config/modulate/api_key
  ```

---

## Outputs

```
Downloads/
├── <Prefix> Parts (29min)/                  ← split-audio.sh output
│   ├── <Prefix> 1 - Part 1.mp4
│   ├── <Prefix> 1 - Part 2.mp4  ...
│   └── Transcripts/                          ← transcribe.py output
│       ├── <Prefix> 1 - Part 1.txt
│       └── ...
├── <Prefix> Transcripts/                     ← consolidate-transcripts.sh output
│   ├── <Prefix> 1.txt   (all its parts joined in order)
│   └── ... one per source recording
└── <Compiled Document Title>.md              ← the final compile step's output
```

---

## Method

### 1. Split
```bash
bin/split-audio.sh ~/Downloads "Faith" 29
```
Splits every `Faith <N>.<ext>` in `~/Downloads` into 29-minute stream-copy parts. Verify
part counts/durations before moving on — `ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration
-of csv=p=0 <file>` on each output, cross-checked against `total_duration / (segment_minutes
* 60)` rounded up.

### 2. Transcribe
```bash
python3 bin/transcribe.py "$HOME/Downloads/Faith Parts (29min)"
```
Run this as a **background** task (it's slow — budget ~1-2 min per 29-minute part) and check
back rather than blocking on it. Test on one file first (`transcribe.py <dir> "Part 1"`) to
confirm the API key and request shape work before committing to the full batch — this is
cheap insurance against discovering an auth/format problem 15 files in.

### 3. Consolidate
```bash
bin/consolidate-transcripts.sh "$HOME/Downloads/Faith Parts (29min)/Transcripts" "Faith"
```
Joins parts back into one transcript per original recording. Spot-check a join boundary
(the point where two parts meet) to confirm it reads as a natural mid-sentence cut, not
mangled or duplicated text.

### 4. Compile
Gather the N consolidated transcripts (from step 3) plus any broader-context recordings.
Use `prompts/compile-teaching.md` — either:
  - **Chat route:** paste the filled-in prompt into an LLM chat, attach all the transcripts.
  - **Agent route:** hand an agent (this skill + the transcripts) and have it follow the
    Structural Rulebook in `prompts/compile-teaching.md` directly, writing the `.md` file
    itself.

Either way, the output must satisfy the Validation Checklist below before considering it done.

---

## Decision Rules


source recording, then **compile** all of it into a single publication-quality document using
an LLM with a specific, load-bearing prompt.

Built and verified on a real 5-part "Faith" sermon series (Pastor Charles Muchemi): 5 source
`.mp4` files (53–99 minutes each) → 17 stream-copy-split parts → 17 real transcriptions via
the Modulate STT API → 5 consolidated per-session transcripts → 1 compiled 6-session teaching
document with correct chronological reordering (the numbered parts were **not** taught in
1-2-3-4-5 order — the compile step had to figure that out from internal evidence).

- "split this audio/video into chunks" + "transcribe it" — the mechanical first half.
- "turn these sermon/lecture/meeting recordings into one document" — the compile step.
- A series of recordings whose *file order* is known to not match the *actual teaching
  order* (very common with sermon series, recurring lecture series, multi-session
  workshops) — this skill's compile step exists specifically for that case.
- "don't leave anything out" + "make it read like [speaker] is talking to the reader" —
  the voice-preservation requirement this skill's prompt is tuned for.

- A single short recording that doesn't need splitting — just transcribe it directly.

  skill is explicitly anti-summary; see the prompt's "do not leave out a thing."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Transcribe every audio/video file in a folder via the Modulate STT batch API.

Usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]

Reads the API key from ~/.config/modulate/api_key (create it with `chmod 600`
BEFORE running this — never hardcode the key in this script or commit it
anywhere). Writes "<name>.txt" into a Transcripts/ subfolder of src_dir.

Idempotent: skips any file that already has a non-empty .txt transcript, so
it's safe to re-run on a folder that new source files keep landing in over
time — only the new ones get transcribed.
"""
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

# Modulate STT — multilingual batch model, synchronous, .mp3/.mp4/.wav/etc,
# 100MB file limit. See https://docs.modulate.ai/get-started/stt for the full
# reference (other endpoints: english-only "vfast" variant, streaming/WebSocket).
API_URL = "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch"
KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/modulate/api_key"

AUDIO_EXTS = (
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".flac",
    ".ogg", ".opus", ".webm", ".aiff", ".mov",
)


def get_api_key() -> str:
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        sys.exit(
            f"API key not found at {KEY_FILE}\n"
            f"Create it first: umask 077 && printf '<your key>' > {KEY_FILE} && chmod 600 {KEY_FILE}"
        )
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Transcribe every audio/video file in a folder via the Modulate STT batch API.

Usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]

Reads the API key from ~/.config/modulate/api_key (create it with `chmod 600`
BEFORE running this — never hardcode the key in this script or commit it
anywhere). Writes "<name>.txt" into a Transcripts/ subfolder of src_dir.

Idempotent: skips any file that already has a non-empty .txt transcript, so
it's safe to re-run on a folder that new source files keep landing in over
time — only the new ones get transcribed.
"""
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import requests

# Modulate STT — multilingual batch model, synchronous, .mp3/.mp4/.wav/etc,
# 100MB file limit. See https://docs.modulate.ai/get-started/stt for the full
# reference (other endpoints: english-only "vfast" variant, streaming/WebSocket).
API_URL = "https://platform.modulate.ai/api/velma-2-stt-batch"
KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config/modulate/api_key"

AUDIO_EXTS = (
    ".mp3", ".mp4", ".wav", ".m4a", ".aac", ".flac",
    ".ogg", ".opus", ".webm", ".aiff", ".mov",
)


def get_api_key() -> str:
    if not KEY_FILE.exists():
        sys.exit(
            f"API key not found at {KEY_FILE}\n"
            f"Create it first: umask 077 && printf '<your key>' > {KEY_FILE} && chmod 600 {KEY_FILE}"
        )
    return KEY_FILE.read_text().strip()


def transcribe(path: Path, api_key: str) -> str:
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        resp = requests.post(
            API_URL,
            headers={"X-API-Key": api_key},
            data={"speaker_diarization": "true"},
            files={"upload_file": (path.name, f, "application/octet-stream")},
            timeout=600,
        )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json().get("text", "")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit("usage: transcribe.py <src_dir> [name_filter]")
    src_dir = Path(sys.argv[1]).expanduser()
    only = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
    out_dir = src_dir / "Transcripts"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    api_key = get_api_key()
    files = sorted(p for p in src_dir.iterdir() if p.suffix.lower() in AUDIO_EXTS)
    if only:
        files = [f for f in files if only in f.name]
    if not files:
        print("No matching audio files found.")
        return

        out_path = out_dir / (path.stem + ".txt")

            print(f"skip (already done): {path.name}")
            continue

            text = transcribe(path, api_key)
        except requests.HTTPError as e:

# Compilation Prompt — Consolidated Transcripts → One Chronological Teaching Document

This is the prompt that produced a genuinely excellent result the first time (a 5-part
"Faith" sermon series compiled into one polished, chronologically-correct, voice-preserving
markdown document). Use it verbatim with placeholders filled in, against an LLM chat that
takes file attachments — or hand this whole file plus the transcripts to an agent with
Write access and ask it to follow §"Structural Rulebook" directly.

## What to attach

1. All N consolidated part-transcripts from `consolidate-transcripts.sh`
   (e.g. `Faith 1.txt` … `Faith 5.txt`).
2. Any broader-context recordings that cover the same material inside a wider session —
   e.g. full meeting/Google-Meet transcripts, if you have them. These aren't required, but
   they're what let the compiling model recover the *true* chronological order and connective
   context the numbered parts alone don't carry.

## The prompt (fill in the brackets)

```
Attached are transcripts of a series on [TOPIC] done by [TEACHER/SPEAKER NAME]
([N range, e.g. 1-5]).

After that, the attached are actual transcripts ([SOURCE, e.g. Google Meet]) from
which the [TOPIC] series was taught (broader in context as they cover entire
sessions as compared to the [N] parts that only cover the teaching).

From the above, generate (compile them into) one teaching on [TOPIC] by [TEACHER
NAME]. .md format. In the file, there should be a chronological flow of the
[TOPIC] series ([N range] doesn't really reflect the manner in which they were
taught — you might find that part 1 was taught after part 4). I think the [N
range] parts nail the teaching well, whereas the other transcripts sort of give
some context. If [TEACHER NAME] made any prayers/declarations/punchlines/
statements be sure to include them in the file, still in a chronological manner.
Also all scripture [or: quotes/citations from your authoritative source] to be
referenced in [NKJV, or your default translation/edition] unless of course
otherwise stated. Format well — headings, titles, bold, italic, etc.

This is a professional [TOPIC] document. Do not leave out a thing. Let it be
such that it is as if [TEACHER NAME] is speaking directly to whoever reads it.
```

The load-bearing phrases, and why each one matters (don't drop these when adapting):
- **"doesn't really reflect the manner in which they were taught"** — this is the single
  instruction that forces real chronological reasoning from internal evidence, instead of
  the model lazily trusting the file numbering. Without it, you get parts 1-5 in that literal
  order, which is very likely *wrong*.
- **"the other transcripts sort of give some context"** — explicitly ranks the two source
  types (numbered teaching parts = primary structure/weight; broader recordings = context
  filler), so the model doesn't over-weight the noisier, less-curated source.
- **"be sure to include them ... still in a chronological manner"** — prayers/declarations/
  punchlines are exactly what a lazy summarizer drops first. Naming the category explicitly
  is what keeps them in.
- **"unless of course otherwise stated"** — the one correctly-scoped escape hatch: don't
  force the standard translation over a quote the speaker explicitly attributed elsewhere.
- **"Do not leave out a thing"** — sets completeness, not summarization, as the goal. This is
  a compile, not a digest.
- **"as if [name] is speaking directly to whoever reads it"** — the instruction that produces
  first/second-person voice preservation instead of third-person academic paraphrase.

---

## Structural Rulebook (reverse-engineered from the reference output)

If you're generating this directly (an agent with Write access, not a separate chat), follow
this structure — it's what the prompt above reliably produces, made explicit:

1. **Title block**: H1 title that names the *theme*, not "Compiled Transcript" (e.g. "The
   Life of Faith"). H2 "A Teaching Series by [Name]". H3 venue/series line. Bold date range.
   Horizontal rule.
2. **Epigraph**: the 1-2 scripture/quotes most central to the whole series, blockquoted,
   italic verse text, em-dash citation, translation noted — set before any narrative content.
3. **"A Note Before We Begin"**: an introductory framing section in the speaker's own first-
   person voice, drawn from their *actual opening remarks in the chronologically-earliest
   session* — not a generic AI-written preamble. If the earliest session has no natural cold
   open, use its first substantive paragraph.
4. **One "# PART [ordinal]: [session's own descriptive title]" section per distinct session**,
   in true chronological order, each carrying:
   - H3 date of that session (only if the source states or clearly implies one — don't invent
     dates)
   - H2 thematic subheadings for each major movement of thought
   - H3 subheadings tied to specific source-passages taught, each immediately followed by
     the passage **quoted from the real reference text** (see Common Pitfalls — not the
     speaker's paraphrase) in a blockquote with citation
   - Body prose that preserves the speaker's actual phrasing, rhetorical repetition, and
     idiom — paraphrase as little as humanly possible; this is a transcript compile, not a
     summary
   - **Bold** for the speaker's key doctrinal/declarative one-liners
   - Blockquotes (same `>` syntax as scripture) for standout verbatim quotes, illustrative
     asides, and personal anecdotes — visually distinct from body prose
   - A dedicated callout subsection for any ritual/ceremonial moment (e.g. "## Communion
     Declaration — [date]"), with the prayer/declaration text preserved close to verbatim
5. **Closing section**: the final prayer/declaration from the chronologically-last session,
   verbatim, blockquoted.
6. **Summary table**: `| Session/Date | Theme | Key Scripture |`, one row per PART, in
   chronological order.
7. **"Core Declarations" list**: 8-10 numbered, pithy one-line doctrinal takeaways distilled
   from across the whole series — these are for skimming/reference, not new content.
8. **Closing pull-quote**: the single most memorable line from the whole series, blockquoted
   with attribution.
9. **Footer**: italic attribution block — compiled-from note, organization, date range,
   speaker name.

### Voice rules
- First person ("I") when the speaker refers to themself; second person ("you") when they
  address the audience directly. The reader should feel spoken to, not informed about.
- Keep the speaker's own structuring language ("Now let me ask you something," "I want you
  to see something here") — it's part of what makes the compile feel authentic rather than
  ghostwritten.
