# Emotional Intelligence
## A Teaching Series by Pastor Charles Muchemi
### Royal Priesthood Embassy · Sunday Services
**A Three-Part Series**

---

> *"He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city."*
> — Proverbs 16:32 (NKJV)

> *"If someone says, 'I love God,' and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who does not love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?"*
> — 1 John 4:20 (NKJV)

---

## A Note Before We Begin

Today I have an interesting subject that we shall be covering, and I guarantee you I am not going to finish this today — I am just going to start. So you must be very careful, because we will be studying the topic: emotional intelligence.

There's a time in the recent past when I promised to do this, and I just realized this particular week that it is time for us to explore and understand what exactly it means to be emotionally intelligent — because it is very easy for you to be intelligent spiritually, yet you are not intelligent emotionally.

When I was posting about this meeting, I wrote something I heard from my father, the Lord. One time he was teaching, and he said that people who are emotionally intelligent end up ruling over people who have a strong IQ and a weak emotional quotient. And I can guarantee you, over time I have verified that statement. I have confirmed that it is true. There is still something that will put a sharp, intelligent person at a disadvantage if they do not master it — and that thing is emotional intelligence.

---

# PART 1: Believer or Christian? Why Character Reveals the Master You Serve

### First Sunday

## Called to Represent, Not Just to Believe

Just to lay a good foundation for where we are going with this topic — I want you to look at your life and begin to identify the things that can make people scared away from desiring your God. I know I am talking to believers. Most of you love God. But check the things in your life that may make your friends, your family, not desire your God. Because I guarantee you, most people out there have not actually had an encounter with God — but they have had an encounter with *you*. And the question is: what resulted from the encounter they had with you?

That is exactly what God did not create us for. Because God intended that when men meet us, they meet God. That is why God does not desire that we do anything to Him that we do not do to man — that we claim to love Him yet do not love man.

The Bible says in the book of Acts that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch. So the question is: who were they before that, yet they had already believed in Jesus Christ?

> *"And when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to pass that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a great many people. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch."*
> — Acts 11:26 (NKJV)

Notice — they assembled with the church, they taught a great many people, for a whole year, and *then* the disciples were first called Christians. It means these people were in the church, but they were not yet Christians. Yet they were believers. There is a difference between being a believer and being a Christian. They are not one and the same thing.

So what is this being Christian? It is simply acting like Christ. The word "Christian" there defines a disciple, not merely a believer — because it is discipleship that made people eventually call them Christians. It is good that you have believed in Jesus Christ. It is good that you have eternal life, and we can guarantee you as a believer that you have a ticket to heaven. But while you live here on earth, will people look at you and desire your God? Will people look at you and know that Christ is your master?

## Love Is the Proof

I've quoted a bit of some verses already — 1 John chapter 4 and verse 20. If someone says "I love God" and hates his brother, he is a liar. There's a challenge being thrown at us here: if you want to claim that you love God, if you want us to verify that you love God, we do not believe by listening to what you say — we believe by looking into your life and finding that you love the people around you.

> *"Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift."*
> — Matthew 5:23–24 (NKJV)

God is not rejecting the fact that you have visited the altar. He is not rejecting that you have made your way there. He actually tells you to leave the gift, because He is expecting you to come back to the altar. But you being at the altar while your brother has something against you is not commendable. It is not acceptable to God.

> *"Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal."*
> — 1 Corinthians 13:1 (NKJV)

You will be at the altar, and according to you, you are saying, "Thank you, Lord, I thank you for your love toward me, I thank you because you are a good God, I thank you because when I pray, you hear me." According to you, that is what you are doing. But on the other end of heaven, what they are hearing is noise. Can you imagine a God who has the ability to hear the prayers of every person on earth — how many billions of people, how many prayers reaching Him in one minute — and He is able to hear all of them? But He separates a kind of prayer, and He says, "All I hear is noise." And that is a prayer coming from a person who does not have love.

## The Character You Cannot Hide

There are things in our lives that do not portray the character of Christ. I like the story about Peter. Peter promises Jesus he is not going to deny Him. Jesus tells him that before the rooster crows, he will deny Him three times.

> *"Assuredly, I say to you that this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." Peter said to Him, "Even if I have to die with You, I will not deny You!" And so said all the disciples.*
> — Matthew 26:34–35 (NKJV)

But it so happens that Peter actually denied Him. And in the process of denying Jesus, people were saying, "We saw you with him," and Peter said, "I do not even know him" — but something was selling him off. It was clear, from the way he was behaving, the way he was speaking, that he had been with Jesus.

> *Then having arrested Him, they led Him and brought Him into the high priest's house. But Peter followed at a distance. Now when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them. And a certain servant girl, seeing him as he sat by the fire, looked intently at him and said, "This man was also with Him." But he denied Him, saying, "Woman, I do not know Him." And after a little while another saw him and said, "You also are of them." But Peter said, "Man, I am not!" Then after about an hour had passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, "Surely this fellow also was with Him, for he is a Galilean." But Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are saying!" Immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.*
> — Luke 22:54–60 (NKJV)

He's trying to deny Jesus Christ, but who he is testifies of the very person he is denying. This is a blessing I want us all to receive — that when people look at us, they don't need us to even open our mouths to testify. Sometimes when they just look at you, they can see Jesus.

There is a day I was somewhere around Safari Park, just standing there, and a Buddhist guy found me and asked, "Pastor, are you going...?" I wondered — why are you calling me Pastor? I don't look like one, not even the way I'm dressed. And this wasn't the first time. I remember walking with Pastor Ryan, and someone who didn't know either of us — we weren't dressed in coats or suits — still called us pastors. I asked Pastor Ryan, "Is this man aware you are a pastor?" He told me, "No." I left testifying, and I told him: this means that if today we were the modern-day Peter, we would also be caught. We try to sit among them, and we'd be caught.

## Believers Who Do Not Look Like Christians

But now, it is also very possible for you to be a believer, going to heaven, speaking in tongues of every kind — and yet when someone looks at you, they cannot really call you a Christian. Trust me — I know people who are born again and they beat their wives. I know people who are born again and they gossip. You find, for example, two people having a very nice friendship; you enroll yourself into their friendship, and the minute you become a third friend, they are no longer friends, because instead of bringing peace, you were like a sword.

I'm not teaching this to say that I am the best. We are also looking to be perfected by God. But it's my responsibility to bring this to you: amongst ourselves, sometimes I just thought something, or I just did something, and I ask myself — did I really do that as a Christian? Could someone check what I thought, check what I did, and still call me a man of God?

Trust me — you may be the reason someone broke up with your friend. They were having a relationship intending to do a wonderful wedding and settle, until you got into their lives, and they believed they were about to do life with the devil, because you set your foot in it — just because maybe you are jealous, you also want to be married but have not been successful for a while, and you don't want to see your friends settled while you have not. How many times have you looked at your friends progressing and made a silent prayer — a desire deep inside your heart that you wish they were not progressing, because their progress made your life look like a joke?

This is why some of you — the reason your own parents don't like you being in the church you go to — is because they know your behaviour in the house. They know how arrogant you are, even to your own parents. They know you're not a responsible person. Meanwhile, I have found parents supporting their children being here because they saw transformation in their own children after they came. When people can see God in how you are living your life, they can easily believe.

## Grace Still Has Consequences

Now, sometimes we fail to realize one thing. It is very possible you are going to heaven even if it does not look like you are a Christian — you are still going to go to heaven. But one thing you must always remember: in life, there are consequences.

> *"Or do you despise the riches of His goodness, forbearance, and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?"*
> — Romans 2:4 (NKJV)

This is why God, no matter what we do, even if we don't portray His character here on earth, still loves us, still extends His kindness to us, still does good to us. But the question is — is this goodness serving its purpose? Because it's supposed to lead us to repentance. Do we end up changing our minds? Do we end up being changed in such a manner that we look like the One who extended His goodness to us? God will continue being patient, long-suffering. But will man be the same to us? Don't forget — God is a Father. He is a loving Father.

This is where you find people like Rahab. With all that they did, they still found their footing in destiny — she is written of in Hebrews 11. But did she experience the consequences of what she did? Yes, she did. If you go and study the life of Eli the priest — a man of God, living for God — yet he did not have sons who portrayed what he believed.

## Wisdom Is Context-Specific

Before I give you these examples — the wisdom of God is context-specific. It means you can be very sharp in business but very dull in marriage.

Solomon was a genius. When you come to the nation of Israel, they had the best-administered kingdom — he never even fought one war. He asked God for wisdom, and he received a kind of wisdom. But there is another form of wisdom he did not receive — a certain context in which we find him in weakness. You can find a very good person doing their thing — maybe a work of art, maybe relating to people, they are very nice, no one can say this person hurt them — but as far as finances go, they don't have wisdom for it. God has given them wisdom to maneuver, to enjoy marriage even without money, but not wisdom for finance. That is the level of wisdom they have attained.

I don't want to get into everything about marriage, but let me say this: when God created man, He first created animals, and Adam lived with them, and only then did God say it is not good for this man to dwell alone. Man was not meant for animals. Man was supposed to be complete by man. When you are getting married to someone, you are not getting married to what they have, you are getting married to *who they are*. Money will facilitate the demands of the relationship, money will make it easy — but the reason people think they need money to enjoy marriage is because the people getting married do not have discernment, do not have emotional intelligence. There is a creature somewhere who will not believe you love them until you buy them a gift, until a certain kind of wedding, because they cannot see beyond what happens in the natural. That is a cover-up for the fallenness of man.

You are also seeing the sons of Jacob — we can as well call them businessmen, but their first business deal was trading their own brother. This is the kind of thing wisdom in one area and its absence in another can produce. Look at David — a man I love, very good in leading a nation, yet his own son Amnon violated his sister Tamar. It is important that you understand: wisdom is context-specific. You can be good in one thing and not good in another. You can run certain things smoothly, yet others are going to rough you up.

> *This is a faithful saying: If a man desires the position of a bishop, he desires a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, of good behavior, hospitable, able to teach; not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous; one who rules his own house well, having his children in submission with all reverence (for if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the church of God?); not a novice, lest being puffed up with pride he fall into the same condemnation as the devil. Moreover he must have a good testimony among those who are outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.*
> — 1 Timothy 3:1–7 (NKJV)

Even reading just to verse 7, you must see what God is saying: the wisdom you need to become a spiritual leader is not the only wisdom you need. You need wisdom to control your emotions, to be hospitable, to know how not to be violent, selfish, or quarrelsome — and wisdom to rule your own house well. This is exactly opposite of what we often find today. This scripture is not just for someone becoming a "bishop" — you are a king and a priest, so you may be given a department to lead. You can derive patterns, you can be excellent — but there is always a problem when it is you relating to other people, if you have not attained this wisdom.

This was Eli — a priest, but he did not have the wisdom he needed to raise his children, and the sons of Eli died before him because of it. This was David with Amnon and Tamar. And this was Jacob — you say you are the Israel of God, you are talking about Jacob — yet he had sons who plotted to kill one of their own, and traded their own brother as their very first business deal.

So I'm going to end today's sermon at that point. But trust me, there is a lot that we need to cover. I didn't even notice I had that much to say. But God has helped us, and we shall continue from there next time.

> *Father, we thank you for every challenge, we thank you for every rebuke. Thank you for correction. We thank you for every purpose your word served us today. We ask you, O Lord, that even as we receive this wisdom from you, you are growing us emotionally, you are maturing us emotionally, that our lives will not testify differently from what you intended them to be a witness of. We thank you because you always help us, even in our weaknesses, in Jesus' mighty name. Amen.*

# PART 2: Seeing Beyond the Action — Discernment, Forgiveness, and the Wisdom of Joseph

### Second Sunday

## Continuing Where We Left Off

I want us to continue with the same discussion we started last Sunday, about emotional intelligence. This is a very interesting topic — you're going to discover a lot of things about yourself, about the people around you, about certain behaviours and patterns as we go. By the time we are done this month, I want to believe God will help each of us to be emotionally intelligent.

Remember — we started in Acts 11:26, and I told you the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch; that it is very easy for you to be a believer going to heaven, but for no one to look at you and call you a Christian. We moved forward to talk about the wisdom of God being context-specific — you can have wisdom in one area and lack it in another, which is not God's will. We read 1 Timothy 3, and saw that God's will for a leader is to exhibit the character of Christ altogether — so you don't have someone who is a wonderful priest to God, like Eli, yet lacks the wisdom to raise children who look like Christ. So you don't become like Jacob, whose children plotted against one of their own. I gave you several examples of people in the Bible where wisdom was present in one area, and lacking in another — David, good in leading a nation, but one son reaping another child, one son rebelling. Solomon, very good at administration, but without the wisdom to remain faithful in his marriage.

## Discernment Is Emotional Intelligence

Today I want to continue that conversation until we see fruit. If you are having a walk with God, it should be notable that you have been with Him. It is very easy to possess gifts, yet be lacking when it comes to the fruit of the Spirit — and this is why so much around the lives of believers begins to fail. We concentrate on giftings and forget the fruits that are essential, not only in our walk with God, but with men.

I don't see many gifts that are going to help you in marriage. Imagine using the gift of working of miracles, or the gift of word of knowledge — these are not what will keep you from divorce. But I know of a gift that can help you have a stable family, and that gift is discernment. What is discernment? It is the ability to understand what is at play — to see beyond what can be seen with the natural eyes, deeper than what meets the eye. Discernment is a supernatural reality — but when we come to social skill, discernment is the same as emotional intelligence. I wanted to show you the relationship, because emotional intelligence is a social skill, and I have been emphasizing that apart from knowing how to walk in the spirit, you need soft skills — learning how to communicate, learning how to manage conflict.

## Gethsemane: Seeing the Heart Behind the Action

> *Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples, "Sit here while I go and pray over there." And He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and He began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed. Then He said to them, "My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch with Me." He went a little farther and fell on His face, and prayed, saying, "O My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as You will." Then He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, "What? Could you not watch with Me one hour? Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."*
> — Matthew 26:36–41 (NKJV)

Notice — the distress did not come upon Him when He had all the disciples with Him, but when He had Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. These were the ones He could be vulnerable to, the ones who could pray with Him. He let them know the season He was in — a very sensitive season, when He needed His friends the most, when He was about to be killed. He asked them to help Him pray, and they slept.

If you were Jesus, what would you call it? Betrayal. "I was there for you when you were going through this, and right now I've called you for only one hour of prayer, and you couldn't do it." But Jesus was able to look beyond the action. He was able to separate the action from the motive in the heart of these people — "the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." You may want to call this a spiritual gift, but let me tell you — this is emotional intelligence. Most of you could not have handled that moment in such a mature way. This was supposed to be an emotional moment, but Jesus looked past the action.

Can you imagine a friend saying a very hurtful thing to you, and you are angry at them? I know most of you have such friends — they don't know how to say things, they "speak their mind," they don't know how to articulate their speech, and you can't see that they did not mean it the way it landed. Don't misunderstand me here — the fact that another person is mature enough to see beyond what you said does not make what you did right. There is a difference — sometimes we say empathy is an expression of love, but sometimes empathy is a sign that you have abandoned yourself. There are people who always expect you to understand them, always expect you to be the mature one. I'm not saying it's right when people do these things — I'm only clarifying, before you think you're justified because someone understood you. Also seek to be the mature one, seek to be the one who understands. And if you're the one who always understands, who is always the mature one — don't get tired. Remain strong.

## Joseph: The Master of Emotional Intelligence

> *But as for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, in order to bring it about as it is this day, to save many people alive.*
> — Genesis 50:20 (NKJV)

This is the life of Joseph — a very mysterious man. If you study Joseph, you're going to learn wisdoms that are, I believe, one of the greatest displays of emotional intelligence I have seen in the Bible. He is looking at his brothers — the people behind every bad thing that happened to him. I believe the very first business the brothers ever conducted, an international business, was selling their own brother. What manner of wickedness is this? And the man they sell goes to another country, becomes excellent in the house of Potiphar, and is accused of something he did not do — he ends up in jail — because a few people decided to betray their own.

And then, one-on-one, not through a Google Meet, he looks at them and says what he says in Genesis 50:20. This is like looking at a terrorist and saying, "You meant evil, but God did not mean evil against me — He meant good."

> *And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are called according to His purpose.*
> — Romans 8:28 (NKJV)

Let me help you understand this verse. It says "all things work together" — the good things and the bad things, all of them work together for good, for those who love God. The only thing we usually think is working for our good is the good thing that happened to us. But this is saying all things — your pastor who is preaching to you, your teacher, that policeman who is arresting you, even that parent who abandoned you — all of them, put together, are working for your good.

This is emotional intelligence being tested. One sign of someone who is not intelligent emotionally: they react to a situation instead of responding. Something happens to us, and instead of sitting down with God to analyze the situation, we begin to complain, we begin throwing stones. It takes not only spiritual maturity but emotional maturity to look at people who cost you pain and see the purposes of God behind it all. That they meant evil does not mean God meant it for evil as well.

If you want to learn forgiveness, look at the life of Joseph — he forgave his brothers and called them into the very palace he was in. He was in charge of their food. Imagine — a man who wanted to kill you is now the one going to the kitchen to cook for you. I'm trying to show you what kind of maturity was in Joseph's life, that he was not tempted to revenge even when he had every opportunity. This is largeness of heart. Can you put your heart aside and allow the purposes of God to continue?

Sometimes people are in pain because someone cheated on them, and I wonder — what is there to cry about? It feels like God just showed you mercy. What if that person had cheated after you were already in marriage, already in that covenant? God just revealed the snake before you entered the promised land. This is why you need discernment.

## The Wisdom to Stay Silent

> *But when the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet justice does not allow to live."*
> — Acts 28:4 (NKJV)

You need the ability to discern — to differentiate between a snake and a piece of wood. Maybe God showed you signs, and you ignored all of them, and then you had to break your service to that relationship, and end up in depression for months.

Can I show you something even greater than forgiveness in the life of Joseph? It is one thing to forgive people. It is another thing not to tell people what those people did to you — because you sustain the wisdom to know that they may never forgive them the same way you did. If you share the weakness of your spouse with people, even in church, you may be able to forgive your spouse and love them and move forward — but there are people who, once you tell them, will always disrespect that person, always dishonor them, because they were not able to forgive the way you did. When people offend me in church, I forgive them — and then one day I'm out doing life and I greet that person very warmly, and I notice the person I'm with is very uncomfortable, even hating that person, because they don't know what I know and forgave. This is why, when people do these things, I don't always tell you. Sometimes the less you know, the better — because if I explain what happened, I will forgive that person, but you will not, and I know it.

Imagine all this time I have not even defined what emotional intelligence is — because I am not looking for a definition first. I want you to understand, and from what you understand, we are going to define it together. Let me end here this morning, and we will continue next week. I'm going to define emotional intelligence for you, and I will teach you how to become intelligent emotionally, how to regulate emotions — because emotional intelligence involves the regulation of emotions; it's part of it.

> *Father, we thank you for teaching us how to live here on earth, how to relate with people, how to have your very character in us expressed through us. We ask you to give us wisdom to always see your purposes beyond the things that happen around us. Help us, even when we are not intelligent emotionally, that we may never sabotage our destinies, that we may never deny you the glory that you deserve. In Jesus' mighty name. Amen.*

# PART 3: The Anatomy of Emotional Intelligence — Definition, Self-Rule, and the Five Marks of Its Absence

### Third Sunday — Last Sunday of the Month

## Continuing Where We Left Off

We have covered quite a lot so far, even if I have not yet given a formal definition — and the reason I did not define it first is because I wanted you to have an understanding of what it is before I did. Last time we saw Jesus Himself showcase His intelligence at Gethsemane, where those who should have prayed with Him slept instead — and what a man not so designed could have called betrayal, Jesus looked at and said, "the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak." Discernment is where you see beyond what the natural eye can see. We read about Joseph, who was able to forgive the very people who brought calamity into his life, and park all of that aside to focus on the good that came from what he experienced. We were able to ask a very important question: can we be in a position where we ignore the pain that happens to us, and focus on the purposes of God?

Today we continue. I really want to hurry a bit, because this is the last Sunday of the month, and I will not be able to cover everything I wanted to cover in relation to emotional intelligence — I will return to this topic when we talk about relationships (and no, not only romantic relationships). One of the areas I really want to focus on today is communication, because your unintelligence in emotions is normally revealed when you are communicating.

## Defining Emotional Intelligence

So I want to define emotional intelligence. If you're writing, you can say:

> *Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognize, understand, manage, and appropriately express your own emotions, while also discerning and responding wisely to the emotions of others, in ways that build relationships, solve problems, and prevent unnecessary harm.*

And another definition of the same thing:

> *Emotional intelligence is the maturity to remain aware of what is happening within you and around you, allowing your feelings to inform your decisions without controlling them, while treating others with understanding, wisdom, and self-control.*

## Ruling Your Spirit

> *He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city.*
> — Proverbs 16:32 (NKJV)

There is such a thing as ruling your spirit — being in charge of what happens inside of you, and in charge of what happens around you. One of the things that shows you are not intelligent emotionally is constant fighting — but we're getting there.

Are you aware the Bible calls *you* a city also? You are a city set on a hill. So when the Bible says "he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city," it means: when the devil wants to overtake you — a city — if you know how to rule your spirit, you find yourself at an advantage. Most times we blame the devil for what we should blame ourselves. Have you seen people lose jobs because of unfiltered speech — "I'm just speaking my mind" — and then come to church and say there is a demon attacking them, that every job they get, they lose within three months? There is no demon there. You just cannot rule your spirit. So when the enemy wants to overtake you, he easily does, because you cannot rule your spirit. There are people who lose every relationship they enter — not because the people they meet are snakes, but because they, themselves, cannot rule their spirit; they have no self-control, so anything that comes to mind, they speak it. It is not that people won't push you to certain extremes — but feeling the necessity to react a certain way is not a justification to react unwisely. The Bible does not say you will never become angry — it says be *slow* to anger.

## Wisdom Over Strength

> *Then I said, "Wisdom is better than strength."*
> — Ecclesiastes 9:16 (NKJV)

When I read this verse, I think of men — because it is men who are strong. There is a way, as men, we can misuse strength and forget wisdom — for example, when men beat their wives, they have remembered strength and forgotten wisdom. When I teach on communication and relationships in future, I'll also teach something on communication across genders — men do not speak the same way as women, and there are things that work in speaking to one that do not work with the other. For example, never criticize a man — it does not work. It works, painfully, for women, but it does not work for men. I'll teach this another time.

## Every Day Is an Audition

This life is very deep. Every single day we walk into minefields of opportunities, interactions, and trials — every person you meet is a test, because life is a complex web of connection, and the tragedy is that most of these connections are unseen. Every room you walk into, every conflict you handle, every authority you encounter, may be a test to your maturity.

> *Behold, I stand here by the well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water. Now let it be that the young woman to whom I say, "Please let down your pitcher that I may drink," and she says, "Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink" — let her be the one whom You have appointed for Your servant Isaac.*
> — Genesis 24:13–14 (NKJV)

This is Abraham's servant, sent to find a wife for Isaac. Many daughters of the city are coming to the well — but remember, he's looking for one. Imagine if Rebekah had come that day with a nasty attitude. Imagine, it is you — a stranger comes and says, "Give me a drink, and my camels too" — and even before you say hello back, your first response is, "Who are you, what do you want?" If you have that kind of attitude, get born again today. There are specific credentials you must attain, because there are certain things God cannot do with you unless you attain them.

Write this down: **every day of your life is an audition.** You may be praying, you may be fasting, but your attitude can be a repellent. There is a man — this is what I normally tell men — don't be quick to tell a woman you want to marry her. Stay around, observe her attitude, see how she treats other people. The minute you tell them, they will behave nicely. Before that, watch how they handle conflict, how they treat people who cannot do anything for them. The quality of your life can completely change because of a single moment, a single decision. You can spend ten years building a life, a career, a marriage — and destroy it in ten seconds, because you couldn't master an immediate emotional reaction. Most people believe their success depends purely on their talents, their qualifications — but talents and gifting open the door; **emotional regulation decides whether you stay in that room.**

## The Credential of Self-Control

There was an assignment given to Moses that was given to another because he lacked a certain credential — self-control. God told him, "Go and speak to the stone," and Moses, instead, struck it. For that, God told him he would not lead the people into the Promised Land — Joshua took over. There are things you will miss in life because you are lacking certain credentials, and mostly, they are closely related to emotional intelligence.

Even further — Moses told God, in Exodus, "Send someone else," and the Bible says the anger of the Lord was kindled against him. Do you think God could not have performed a miracle so that Moses would speak well? He did exactly that kind of miracle later with Isaiah, with a coal of fire touching his lips. Why not for Moses? Because God said, "Aaron will go with you; he shall speak, and I will teach *you*." Some of you are asking for a miracle. You need to be taught how to speak.

## The Cost of an Irreversible Moment

I was watching a movie — an honest FBI agent, one of the good ones, not corrupt. His badge is taken because of something that happened, and when he goes to collect it, his senior — a woman — says something so offensive that he strikes her, one motion, and she falls and dies. Now this good cop has to look for someone to help him hide it, because murder is a direct ticket to life imprisonment. He compromised, even as a good cop, because in one moment he did something he could not reverse. He does not know how to resurrect someone.

This is the tragic nature of emotional reaction — most times, it is permanent. Once the word has left your mouth, once the email is sent, once the message is sent, once the bridge is burned, you cannot recall it. **You are left sitting in the ashes of the fire you lit just to warm your ego — for five seconds.**

## Unfiltered Speech Is Not Bravery

We live in a culture that worships unfiltered speech — "I speak my mind," "I say it as it is," "I'm just being real." Let's call this what it is: it is not bravery, it is foolishness. **Unfiltered speech is a mark of an undisciplined mind.** It assumes that everything that comes to your mind needs an audience, that every feeling that comes to your chest needs a microphone. (I'm speaking to the Gen Zs — I am very much aware.) There are people in your life — a family member, a colleague, your boss — who are not going to treat you nicely, who will be difficult, demanding, unfair. But their bad behaviour does not give you permission to ruin your own future. Sometimes we think we know our rights — but who told you that you can express your rights to anyone, anywhere, regardless of who is holding the door you need to enter tomorrow? When your boss tests your patience, **biting your tongue is not cowardice — it is strategic wisdom.**

Some of these difficult people are critically important to your destiny. I remember someone — let's call him a man who worked in one company and lied to his boss about being sick, to go interview at another — only to find, in the interview room, that it was a branch of the same company, and his own boss sitting on the panel. He lost both jobs. You never know when the person you're insulting in traffic, or lying to, is the very one seated in the room of your next decision.

## Why You Don't Fire Everyone Who Frustrates You

Even when you are the boss, there are people you are not meant to fire, no matter how difficult they are — because sometimes they are holding a skill that will push your company, or your destiny, to the next level. I heard a story from a man they call Pastor Apoju — in his office, a woman was causing chaos, and every employee told him, "You need to fire this woman." But he had discernment, and every time he thought of it, he felt a restraint not to. After some time she left, went abroad, and was hired at a television station as a programmer — the one who decides who ministers on air. And it happened that Pastor Apoju was given that very slot — that is how he went, for the first time, to minister on television.

There are people even I have not chased out of ministry when others thought I should — people who have planted scandals against me, and God has shown me before time, and yet I impart grace on them in the next service, and someone is offended, wondering why I am not acting. I have heard people say crazy things about me, and I know they lied — but I don't always tell them I know.

> *He who pampers his servant from childhood will have him as a son in the end.*
> — Proverbs 29:21 (NKJV)

Some of these people, we are bearing them because we want them to become sons in the end. We understand today you are a gossiper, we understand today you are a snake — but we are looking to have you as a son in the end. That is why we don't get tired with certain people. There is a way emotional restraint will allow you to look past the friction and see the bigger picture, and that action might position you for a major breakthrough. **Wisdom knows that not every provocation deserves a response.**

## The Anatomy of Emotional Unintelligence

Let me give you the anatomy — the science — of emotional unintelligence.

**1. Constant fighting.** The easiest thing to do in the flesh is to fight. It requires zero discipline to scream, to slam doors, to trade insults — it takes far less energy to burn a bridge than to build one. When children are growing, in their first years they respond only through impulse — if they're hungry or angry, they cry, they scream — because their minds have not developed to a place where they can judge rightly. That is why we're taken to school: so our minds develop to a point where they can find purpose for our emotions. **True intelligence is the ability to sit down, assess a situation, and talk through it without escalation.**

**2. Reaction over reflection.** A person who is not emotionally intelligent cannot handle honest feedback, no matter how lovingly it is packaged. The moment correction comes, the walls go up. They react with defensiveness instead of reflecting with humility, because they view feedback as an attack on their character rather than an invitation to grow.

**3. Making everything about yourself.** Have you met people who turn every conversation into a competition of suffering? You tell them what you're going through, and they want to compete that theirs is worse — especially about money. What kind of trophy are you looking to inherit? They cannot allow you to express yourself, cannot hear you out, because they're quick to interrupt so they can tell their own story. This is an inability to extend empathy, because you want your own ego validated.

**4. Weaponized history.** When a foolish person is clearly proven wrong, they will never look you in the eye and say, "I'm sorry." Instead, they dig up a ghost from your past: "Is this not the same thing you did to me last year?" They weaponize history because they lack the courage to own their present failure.

**5. Crossing emotional boundaries.** There are people who can't even tell when they're overstepping — they don't know how to read the room, they're missing social cues entirely, with a total lack of awareness of the environment they're in.

## The Closing Charge

The next time you feel the urge to say your mind, or burn a bridge, stop and ask yourself this single question:

> **Am I about to sacrifice ten years of my life, of my future, just to win ten seconds of an argument?**

The last thing I will say: **do not let your emotions draft the script of your life.**

> *Father God, we thank you for being a good God unto us. Thank you for teaching us how to control, how to regulate our emotions. Thank you for being mindful of us. There is no one better than you. You have shown us mercy, and we ask you to give us the same grace to show others mercy. Help us to be kind to others. Help us to see things as you see them. Help us to judge as you judge. In Jesus' mighty name. Amen.*

# PART 1: Believer or Christian? Why Character Reveals the Master You Serve

### First Sunday

## Called to Represent, Not Just to Believe

Just to lay a good foundation for where we are going with this topic — I want you to look at your life and begin to identify the things that can make people scared away from desiring your God. I know I am talking to believers. Most of you love God. But check the things in your life that may make your friends, your family, not desire your God. Because I guarantee you, most people out there have not actually had an encounter with God — but they have had an encounter with *you*. And the question is: what resulted from the encounter they had with you?

That is exactly what God did not create us for. Because God intended that when men meet us, they meet God. That is why God does not desire that we do anything to Him that we do not do to man — that we claim to love Him yet do not love man.

The Bible says in the book of Acts that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch. So the question is: who were they before that, yet they had already believed in Jesus Christ?

> *"And when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to pass that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a great many people. And the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch."*
> — Acts 11:26 (NKJV)

Notice — they assembled with the church, they taught a great many people, for a whole year, and *then* the disciples were first called Christians. It means these people were in the church, but they were not yet Christians. Yet they were believers. There is a difference between being a believer and being a Christian. They are not one and the same thing.

So what is this being Christian? It is simply acting like Christ. The word "Christian" there defines a disciple, not merely a believer — because it is discipleship that made people eventually call them Christians. It is good that you have believed in Jesus Christ. It is good that you have eternal life, and we can guarantee you as a believer that you have a ticket to heaven. But while you live here on earth, will people look at you and desire your God? Will people look at you and know that Christ is your master?

## Love Is the Proof

I've quoted a bit of some verses already — 1 John chapter 4 and verse 20. If someone says "I love God" and hates his brother, he is a liar. There's a challenge being thrown at us here: if you want to claim that you love God, if you want us to verify that you love God, we do not believe by listening to what you say — we believe by looking into your life and finding that you love the people around you.

> *"Therefore if you bring your gift to the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift."*
> — Matthew 5:23–24 (NKJV)

God is not rejecting the fact that you have visited the altar. He is not rejecting that you have made your way there. He actually tells you to leave the gift, because He is expecting you to come back to the altar. But you being at the altar while your brother has something against you is not commendable. It is not acceptable to God.

> *"Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal."*
> — 1 Corinthians 13:1 (NKJV)

You will be at the altar, and according to you, you are saying, "Thank you, Lord, I thank you for your love toward me, I thank you because you are a good God, I thank you because when I pray, you hear me." According to you, that is what you are doing. But on the other end of heaven, what they are hearing is noise. Can you imagine a God who has the ability to hear the prayers of every person on earth — how many billions of people, how many prayers reaching Him in one minute — and He is able to hear all of them? But He separates a kind of prayer, and He says, "All I hear is noise." And that is a prayer coming from a person who does not have love.

## The Character You Cannot Hide

There are things in our lives that do not portray the character of Christ. I like the story about Peter. Peter promises Jesus he is not going to deny Him. Jesus tells him that before the rooster crows, he will deny Him three times.

> *"Assuredly, I say to you that this night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." Peter said to Him, "Even if I have to die with You, I will not deny You!" And so said all the disciples.*
> — Matthew 26:34–35 (NKJV)

But it so happens that Peter actually denied Him. And in the process of denying Jesus, people were saying, "We saw you with him," and Peter said, "I do not even know him" — but something was selling him off. It was clear, from the way he was behaving, the way he was speaking, that he had been with Jesus.

> *Then having arrested Him, they led Him and brought Him into the high priest's house. But Peter followed at a distance. Now when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and sat down together, Peter sat among them. And a certain servant girl, seeing him as he sat by the fire, looked intently at him and said, "This man was also with Him." But he denied Him, saying, "Woman, I do not know Him." And after a little while another saw him and said, "You also are of them." But Peter said, "Man, I am not!" Then after about an hour had passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, "Surely this fellow also was with Him, for he is a Galilean." But Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are saying!" Immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.*
> — Luke 22:54–60 (NKJV)

He's trying to deny Jesus Christ, but who he is testifies of the very person he is denying. This is a blessing I want us all to receive — that when people look at us, they don't need us to even open our mouths to testify. Sometimes when they just look at you, they can see Jesus.

There is a day I was somewhere around Safari Park, just standing there, and a Buddhist guy found me and asked, "Pastor, are you going...?" I wondered — why are you calling me Pastor? I don't look like one, not even the way I'm dressed. And this wasn't the first time. I remember walking with Pastor Ryan, and someone who didn't know either of us — we weren't dressed in coats or suits — still called us pastors. I asked Pastor Ryan, "Is this man aware you are a pastor?" He told me, "No." I left testifying, and I told him: this means that if today we were the modern-day Peter, we would also be caught. We try to sit among them, and we'd be caught.

## Believers Who Do Not Look Like Christians

But now, it is also very possible for you to be a believer, going to heaven, speaking in tongues of every kind — and yet when someone looks at you, they cannot really call you a Christian. Trust me — I know people who are born again and they beat their wives. I know people who are born again and they gossip. You find, for example, two people having a very nice friendship; you enroll yourself into their friendship, and the minute you become a third friend, they are no longer friends, because instead of bringing peace, you were like a sword.

I'm not teaching this to say that I am the best. We are also looking to be perfected by God. But it's my responsibility to bring this to you: amongst ourselves, sometimes I just thought something, or I just did something, and I ask myself — did I really do that as a Christian? Could someone check what I thought, check what I did, and still call me a man of God?

Trust me — you may be the reason someone broke up with your friend. They were having a relationship intending to do a wonderful wedding and settle, until you got into their lives, and they believed they were about to do life with the devil, because you set your foot in it — just because maybe you are jealous, you also want to be married but have not been successful for a while, and you don't want to see your friends settled while you have not. How many times have you looked at your friends progressing and made a silent prayer — a desire deep inside your heart that you wish they were not progressing, because their progress made your life look like a joke?

This is why some of you — the reason your own parents don't like you being in the church you go to — is because they know your behaviour in the house. They know how arrogant you are, even to your own parents. They know you're not a responsible person. Meanwhile, I have found parents supporting their children being here because they saw transformation in their own children after they came. When people can see God in how you are living your life, they can easily believe.

## Grace Still Has Consequences

Now, sometimes we fail to realize one thing. It is very possible you are going to heaven even if it does not look like you are a Christian — you are still going to go to heaven. But one thing you must always remember: in life, there are consequences.

> *"Or do you despise the riches of His goodness, forbearance, and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?"*
> — Romans 2:4 (NKJV)

This is why God, no matter what we do, even if we don't portray His character here on earth, still loves us, still extends His kindness to us, still does good to us. But the question is — is this goodness serving its purpose? Because it's supposed to lead us to repentance. Do we end up changing our minds? Do we end up being changed in such a manner that we look like the One who extended His goodness to us? God will continue being patient, long-suffering. But will man be the same to us? Don't forget — God is a Father. He is a loving Father.

This is where you find people like Rahab. With all that they did, they still found their footing in destiny — she is written of in Hebrews 11. But did she experience the consequences of what she did? Yes, she did. If you go and study the life of Eli the priest — a man of God, living for God — yet he did not have sons who portrayed what he believed.

## Wisdom Is Context-Specific

Before I give you these examples — the wisdom of God is context-specific. It means you can be very sharp in business but very dull in marriage.

Solomon was a genius. When you come to the nation of Israel, they had the best-administered kingdom — he never even fought one war. He asked God for wisdom, and he received a kind of wisdom. But there is another form of wisdom he did not receive — a certain context in which we find him in weakness. You can find a very good person doing their thing — maybe a work of art, maybe relating to people, they are very nice, no one can say this person hurt them — but as far as finances go, they don't have wisdom for it. God has given them wisdom to maneuver, to enjoy marriage even without money, but not wisdom for finance. That is the level of wisdom they have attained.

I don't want to get into everything about marriage, but let me say this: when God created man, He first created animals, and Adam lived with them, and only then did God say it is not good for this man to dwell alone. Man was not meant for animals. Man was supposed to be complete by man. When you are getting married to someone, you are not getting married to what they have, you are getting married to *who they are*. Money will facilitate the demands of the relationship, money will make it easy — but the reason people think they need money to enjoy marriage is because the people getting married do not have discernment, do not have emotional intelligence. There is a creature somewhere who will not believe you love them until you buy them a gift, until a certain kind of wedding, because they cannot see beyond what happens in the natural. That is a cover-up for the fallenness of man.

You are also seeing the sons of Jacob — we can as well call them businessmen, but their first business deal was trading their own brother. This is the kind of thing wisdom in one area and its absence in another can produce. Look at David — a man I love, very good in leading a nation, yet his own son Amnon violated his sister Tamar. It is important that you understand: wisdom is context-specific. You can be good in one thing and not good in another. You can run certain things smoothly, yet others are going to rough you up.

> *This is a faithful saying: If a man desires the position of a bishop, he desires a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, of good behavior, hospitable, able to teach; not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous; one who rules his own house well, having his children in submission with all reverence (for if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the church of God?); not a novice, lest being puffed up with pride he fall into the same condemnation as the devil. Moreover he must have a good testimony among those who are outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.*
> — 1 Timothy 3:1–7 (NKJV)

Even reading just to verse 7, you must see what God is saying: the wisdom you need to become a spiritual leader is not the only wisdom you need. You need wisdom to control your emotions, to be hospitable, to know how not to be violent, selfish, or quarrelsome — and wisdom to rule your own house well. This is exactly opposite of what we often find today. This scripture is not just for someone becoming a "bishop" — you are a king and a priest, so you may be given a department to lead. You can derive patterns, you can be excellent — but there is always a problem when it is you relating to other people, if you have not attained this wisdom.

This was Eli — a priest, but he did not have the wisdom he needed to raise his children, and the sons of Eli died before him because of it. This was David with Amnon and Tamar. And this was Jacob — you say you are the Israel of God, you are talking about Jacob — yet he had sons who plotted to kill one of their own, and traded their own brother as their very first business deal.

So I'm going to end today's sermon at that point. But trust me, there is a lot that we need to cover. I didn't even notice I had that much to say. But God has helped us, and we shall continue from there next time.

> *Father, we thank you for every challenge, we thank you for every rebuke. Thank you for correction. We thank you for every purpose your word served us today. We ask you, O Lord, that even as we receive this wisdom from you, you are growing us emotionally, you are maturing us emotionally, that our lives will not testify differently from what you intended them to be a witness of. We thank you because you always help us, even in our weaknesses, in Jesus' mighty name. Amen.*

# PART 2: Seeing Beyond the Action — Discernment, Forgiveness, and the Wisdom of Joseph

### Second Sunday

## Continuing Where We Left Off

I want us to continue with the same discussion we started last Sunday, about emotional intelligence. This is a very interesting topic — you're going to discover a lot of things about yourself, about the people around you, about certain behaviours and patterns as we go. By the time we are done this month, I want to believe God will help each of us to be emotionally intelligent.

Remember — we started in Acts 11:26, and I told you the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch; that it is very easy for you to be a believer going to heaven, but for no one to look at you and call you a Christian. We moved forward to talk about the wisdom of God being context-specific — you can have wisdom in one area and lack it in another, which is not God's will. We read 1 Timothy 3, and saw that God's will for a leader is to exhibit the character of Christ altogether — so you don't have someone who is a wonderful priest to God, like Eli, yet lacks the wisdom to raise children who look like Christ. So you don't become like Jacob, whose children plotted against one of their own. I gave you several examples of people in the Bible where wisdom was present in one area, and lacking in another — David, good in leading a nation, but one son reaping another child, one son rebelling. Solomon, very good at administration, but without the wisdom to remain faithful in his marriage.

## Discernment Is Emotional Intelligence

Today I want to continue that conversation until we see fruit. If you are having a walk with God, it should be notable that you have been with Him. It is very easy to possess gifts, yet be lacking when it comes to the fruit of the Spirit — and this is why so much around the lives of believers begins to fail. We concentrate on giftings and forget the fruits that are essential, not only in our walk with God, but with men.

I don't see many gifts that are going to help you in marriage. Imagine using the gift of working of miracles, or the gift of word of knowledge — these are not what will keep you from divorce. But I know of a gift that can help you have a stable family, and that gift is discernment. What is discernment? It is the ability to understand what is at play — to see beyond what can be seen with the natural eyes, deeper than what meets the eye. Discernment is a supernatural reality — but when we come to social skill, discernment is the same as emotional intelligence. I wanted to show you the relationship, because emotional intelligence is a social skill, and I have been emphasizing that apart from knowing how to walk in the spirit, you need soft skills — learning how to communicate, learning how to manage conflict.

## Gethsemane: Seeing the Heart Behind the Action

> *Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples, "Sit here while I go and pray over there." And He took with Him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and He began to be sorrowful and deeply distressed. Then He said to them, "My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, even to death. Stay here and watch with Me." He went a little farther and fell on His face, and prayed, saying, "O My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as You will." Then He came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, "What? Could you not watch with Me one hour? Watch and pray, lest you enter into temptation. The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak."*
> — Matthew 26:36–41 (NKJV)

Notice — the distress did not come upon Him when He had all the disciples with Him, but when He had Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. These were the ones He could be vulnerable to, the ones who could pray with Him. He let them know the season He was in — a very sensitive season, when He needed His friends the most, when He was about to be killed. He asked them to help Him pray, and they slept.

If you were Jesus, what would you call it? Betrayal. "I was there for you when you were going through this, and right now I've called you for only one hour of prayer, and you couldn't do it." But Jesus was able to look beyond the action. He was able to separate the action from the motive in the heart of these people — "the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak." You may want to call this a spiritual gift, but let me tell you — this is emotional intelligence. Most of you could not have handled that moment in such a mature way. This was supposed to be an emotional moment, but Jesus looked past the action.

Can you imagine a friend saying a very hurtful thing to you, and you are angry at them? I know most of you have such friends — they don't know how to say things, they "speak their mind," they don't know how to articulate their speech, and you can't see that they did not mean it the way it landed. Don't misunderstand me here — the fact that another person is mature enough to see beyond what you said does not make what you did right. There is a difference — sometimes we say empathy is an expression of love, but sometimes empathy is a sign that you have abandoned yourself. There are people who always expect you to understand them, always expect you to be the mature one. I'm not saying it's right when people do these things — I'm only clarifying, before you think you're justified because someone understood you. Also seek to be the mature one, seek to be the one who understands. And if you're the one who always understands, who is always the mature one — don't get tired. Remain strong.

## Joseph: The Master of Emotional Intelligence

> *But as for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, in order to bring it about as it is this day, to save many people alive.*
> — Genesis 50:20 (NKJV)

This is the life of Joseph — a very mysterious man. If you study Joseph, you're going to learn wisdoms that are, I believe, one of the greatest displays of emotional intelligence I have seen in the Bible. He is looking at his brothers — the people behind every bad thing that happened to him. I believe the very first business the brothers ever conducted, an international business, was selling their own brother. What manner of wickedness is this? And the man they sell goes to another country, becomes excellent in the house of Potiphar, and is accused of something he did not do — he ends up in jail — because a few people decided to betray their own.

And then, one-on-one, not through a Google Meet, he looks at them and says what he says in Genesis 50:20. This is like looking at a terrorist and saying, "You meant evil, but God did not mean evil against me — He meant good."

> *And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are called according to His purpose.*
> — Romans 8:28 (NKJV)

Let me help you understand this verse. It says "all things work together" — the good things and the bad things, all of them work together for good, for those who love God. The only thing we usually think is working for our good is the good thing that happened to us. But this is saying all things — your pastor who is preaching to you, your teacher, that policeman who is arresting you, even that parent who abandoned you — all of them, put together, are working for your good.

This is emotional intelligence being tested. One sign of someone who is not intelligent emotionally: they react to a situation instead of responding. Something happens to us, and instead of sitting down with God to analyze the situation, we begin to complain, we begin throwing stones. It takes not only spiritual maturity but emotional maturity to look at people who cost you pain and see the purposes of God behind it all. That they meant evil does not mean God meant it for evil as well.

If you want to learn forgiveness, look at the life of Joseph — he forgave his brothers and called them into the very palace he was in. He was in charge of their food. Imagine — a man who wanted to kill you is now the one going to the kitchen to cook for you. I'm trying to show you what kind of maturity was in Joseph's life, that he was not tempted to revenge even when he had every opportunity. This is largeness of heart. Can you put your heart aside and allow the purposes of God to continue?

Sometimes people are in pain because someone cheated on them, and I wonder — what is there to cry about? It feels like God just showed you mercy. What if that person had cheated after you were already in marriage, already in that covenant? God just revealed the snake before you entered the promised land. This is why you need discernment.

## The Wisdom to Stay Silent

> *But when the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped the sea, yet justice does not allow to live."*
> — Acts 28:4 (NKJV)

You need the ability to discern — to differentiate between a snake and a piece of wood. Maybe God showed you signs, and you ignored all of them, and then you had to break your service to that relationship, and end up in depression for months.

Can I show you something even greater than forgiveness in the life of Joseph? It is one thing to forgive people. It is another thing not to tell people what those people did to you — because you sustain the wisdom to know that they may never forgive them the same way you did. If you share the weakness of your spouse with people, even in church, you may be able to forgive your spouse and love them and move forward — but there are people who, once you tell them, will always disrespect that person, always dishonor them, because they were not able to forgive the way you did. When people offend me in church, I forgive them — and then one day I'm out doing life and I greet that person very warmly, and I notice the person I'm with is very uncomfortable, even hating that person, because they don't know what I know and forgave. This is why, when people do these things, I don't always tell you. Sometimes the less you know, the better — because if I explain what happened, I will forgive that person, but you will not, and I know it.

Imagine all this time I have not even defined what emotional intelligence is — because I am not looking for a definition first. I want you to understand, and from what you understand, we are going to define it together. Let me end here this morning, and we will continue next week. I'm going to define emotional intelligence for you, and I will teach you how to become intelligent emotionally, how to regulate emotions — because emotional intelligence involves the regulation of emotions; it's part of it.

We ask you to give us wisdom to always see your purposes beyond the things that happen around us.
